title: Kroatialainen Klara Bošnjak Fabijanić viettää eläkepäiviä tipujen ja älypuhelimen kanssa ja muistelee hyvällä Titon aikoja
content:
Autioituneiden rakennusten ikkunoista kurkottaa vihreinä rehottavia puiden oksia. Tienviertä reunustavat talot, joiden katot ovat romahtamaisillaan. Osa taloista on jäänyt keskeneräisiksi, jotkut seisovat tyhjillään, toisissa asutaan yhä.

Pohjois-Kroatian maaseutu on paikoittain karua katseltavaa: muuttoliike kaupunkeihin ja ulkomaille käy kuumana samalla, kun kylät pysyvät vaivoin pystyssä iäkkäiden asukkaiden ja satunnaisten paluumuuttajien ansiosta. Yksi tällaisista on 77-vuotias Klara Bošnjak Fabijanić.

”Tiesin aina, että eläkkeelle jäätyäni muuttaisin takaisin omaan pieneen kylääni.”

Kitinä on kova, kun Bošnjak Fabijanić nostaa sisäpihan kaivosta ämpärillisen kukkienkasteluvettä Unkarin rajalla, Drava-joen eteläpuolella, sijaitsevassa Podravska Moslavinan kylässä.

Sisällä olisi nykyisin myös juoksevaa vettä, mutta Bošnjak Fabijanić käyttää piha-askareisiin mieluummin samaa kaivoa, josta hän on nostanut vedet vuosikymmenten ajan.

Podravska Moslavina on Bošnjak Fabijanićin kotikylä ja koti, jossa hän asuu, hänen lapsuudenkotinsa.

Nyt paikalla on myös hänen tyttärensä, Marija Fabijani.

”Tämä paikka tuo minulle rauhan”, hän sanoo katsellen raukeana ympärilleen.

title: NASA’s Swift telescope has burned up, months after a robot sent to save it failed – here’s why it’s so hard to boost a satellite
content:
NASA’s Neil Gehrels Swift Observatory took its last look at the sky on Oct. 20, 2026, while orbiting about 171 miles (275 kilometers) above Earth. NASA ended the telescope’s mission three days later, because Swift had sunk so low that drag from the thin air there meant its telescopes couldn’t hold steady. The telescope reentered the atmosphere on Nov. 4 above the North Sumatra region of Indonesia and largely burned up, an abrupt ending to two decades spent observing powerful cosmic explosions.

Swift’s reentry comes after a failed rescue mission in the summer of 2026. LINK, a commercial robotic spacecraft sent to raise Swift into a safer orbit, reentered Earth’s atmosphere in September. The machine designed to save a falling satellite burned up first.

As a Ph.D. candidate in aerospace engineering, I know that rescuing satellites is hard. I research how spacecraft approach and capture satellites, including objects that tumble uncontrollably.

Swift’s loss points to a new hazard for the young industry that repairs, refuels and moves spacecraft around in orbit. If something goes wrong, the spacecraft doing the rescuing can become another problem.

title: Holopainen: Jääkiekko on Venäjälle osa valtion propagandaa
content:
Vihreiden kansanedustaja Mari Holopainen pitää Venäjän mahdollista pääsyä takaisin jääkiekon MM-kisoihin erittäin vaarallisena kehityksenä. Urheilun vetoomustuomioistuin CAS näytti Venäjän osallistumiselle vihreää valoa viime perjantaina.

CAS:in päätös ei koske vain Saksan jääkiekon MM-kisoja ensi toukokuussa vaan kaikkia Kansainvälisen jääkiekkoliiton MM-turnauksia vuodesta 2027 alkaen. Ensimmäisenä vuorossa on jo vuodenvaihteessa Kanadassa pelattava alle 20-vuotiaiden MM-turnaus.

"Venäjä käy yhä hyökkäyssotaa Ukrainassa. Jääkiekko on Venäjälle paljon enemmän kuin urheilulaji, se on osa valtion propagandaa. On väärin normalisoida hyökkäyssotaa käyvän maan osallistuminen kisoihin", Holopainen sanoo vihreiden tiedotteessa.

Tänään uutisoitiin, että MM-kisojen pitkäaikainen pääsponsori Skoda Auto harkitsee nyt vetäytymistä turnauksen sponsoroinnista. Tähän mennessä useat jääkiekkomaajoukkueet ovat ilmoittaneet vastustavansa Venäjän paluuta. Suomen lisäksi Ruotsi, Tshekki, Norja, Tanska ja Latvia eivät aio pelata Venäjää vastaan.

Holopaisen mukaan vastuu tilanteesta ei saa jäädä liikaa urheilujärjestöjen, kuten Suomen Jääkiekkoliiton ja Kansainvälisen jääkiekkoliitto IIHF:n varaan.

title: Q&A: What is the Brazil-led ‘deforestation roadmap’?
content:
• What is a deforestation ‘roadmap’?
  • What does the roadmap say about reducing deforestation?
  • Why did some countries not sign onto the roadmap at COP30?
  • What are the barriers to implementing a deforestation roadmap? 

    • On 3 November, the Brazilian presidency of the COP30 climate talks released its long-awaited “roadmap” on ending deforestation. 

    Ahead of the Belém summit, Brazilian president Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva made a call for a “roadmap” to halt and reverse deforestation.

    Although this voluntary roadmap was outside the COP’s official agenda, it snowballed into a rallying point at the “Amazon” COP.

    Some 93 countries called for a reference to a new roadmap for ending deforestation to be part of COP30’s formal negotiated outcome.

    However, at the end of the summit, the COP30 presidency announced that there was not the consensus needed for the deforestation roadmap to be part of the final text – but that Brazil would work to create a voluntary roadmap outside of the UN climate process.

    This call was answered by 18 countries and four negotiating blocs that offered their inputs on the roadmap, along with scores of NGOs, research centres and other groups.

title: Museum Shop Trends: Five Ideas to Test
content:
Museum shops can introduce visitors to local makers, extend an exhibition’s story and generate income for the institution. They also have to make practical retail decisions about stock, pricing, access and the time available to their teams.

A useful starting point is to choose one change that fits your museum and test it. Better product information, a small local-maker range or clearer online collection options may be more useful than an expensive new retail feature.

Here are five areas to consider when developing a museum shop, with examples and questions to help you decide what is worth trying.

Responsible sourcing starts with details: materials, packaging, manufacturing and the evidence behind the supplier’s claims. A museum shop can help customers understand those details, but it should avoid calling a product sustainable without explaining why.

The British Museum shop provides a concrete example. Its Great Wave foldable tote bag is described as being woven from 100% recycled polyester and is inspired by Hokusai’s print. The product page gives a material specification and a collection connection. That is more useful to a buyer than a broad environmental label.

title: Why the weirdest game of 2026 is also one of my favourites
content:

• Don’t get Pushing Buttons delivered to your inbox? Sign up here

Earlier this year, I was stuck in hospital for several days, fuzzy on pain medication and bored out of my mind, with nothing but a Steam Deck for company. In the middle of one of those long nights, unable to sleep, I played a game called Titanium Court. It’s a strange creation that looks like it was made for the ZX Spectrum and reads like a postmodern Shakespeare adaptation – a compelling mix of strategy game and match-3 where you rearrange battlefields by matching tiles, before sending tiny lo-fi fairy armies to their deaths.

title: Asuntokauppa digitalisoituu ympäri Suomen: sähköisten kauppojen osuus kasvoi kaikilla alueilla
content:
Digitaalinen asuntokauppa DIASin ja Tilastokeskuksen tietoihin perustuva alueellinen vertailu osoittaa digitaalisen asuntokaupan yleistyvän laajasti eri puolilla Suomea. Tammi–syyskuussa digitaalisen kaupanteon osuus kasvoi jokaisella Tilastokeskuksen erikseen tilastoimalla alueella viime vuoden samaan ajanjaksoon verrattuna. Eniten, 17 prosenttiyksikköä, osuus kasvoi Pohjois-Suomessa. Pääkaupunkiseudulla ja kehyskunnissa kasvu oli kummassakin noin 15 prosenttiyksikköä.

Alueiden välillä on kuitenkin yhä suuria eroja asuntokaupan digitalisoitumisessa. Korkeimmillaan digitaalisten kauppojen osuus kaikista alueellisista välittäjien tekemistä asunto-osakekaupoista on jo yli 80 prosenttia, kun taas joillakin alueilla vielä noin puolet välittäjien kaupoista syntyy pankin konttorissa ja puolet sähköisesti.

Tammi–syyskuun aikana digitaalisten asunto-osakekauppojen määrä kasvoi Suomessa edellisvuoteen nähden 9 prosenttia. Samaan aikaan välittäjien tekemien asunto-osakekauppojen määrä laski noin 11 prosenttia. Kokonaisuutena DIAS-kauppojen osuus välittäjien tekemistä vanhojen asunto-osakkeiden kaupoista oli syyskuussa 71 prosenttia, kun se vuotta aiemmin oli 57 prosenttia.

title: Kasvatusalan ammattilaisilla hyvät mahdollisuudet edistää väestön liikkumista – koulutus ei vielä anna siihen riittäviä valmiuksia
content:
Valtaosa väestöstä ei täytä liikkumissuosituksia ja liikkuu terveytensä kannalta liian vähän. Väestön liikkumisen edistämiseksi tarvitaan mukaan kaikki hallinnonalat. Erityisesti mukaan tarvitaan koulutuspolitiikka, jotta kasvatus- ja opetusammattilaiset osaisivat omassa työssään edistää liikkumista ja liikuntaa.

Valtion liikuntaneuvoston tilaaman selvityksen mukaan liikkuminen on tunnistettavissa useimmissa tarkastelluissa kasvatusalan koulutuksissa, mutta liikkuminen muodostaa vain harvoin kaikille opiskelijoille yhteisen, koulutuksen eri osiin ulottuvan osaamisalueen. Liikkuminen keskittyy usein yksittäiseen opintojaksoon tai valinnaiseen kokonaisuuteen tai jää opetuksen käytännön toteutustavaksi.

Selvityksen kyselyyn vastanneet kasvatusalan ammattilaiset pitävät ammattialan roolia merkittävänä liikkumiseen ohjaamisessa. Vastaajat myös toivovat liikkumisen näkyvän tutkinnon tavoitteissa ja tai sisällöissä nykyistä enemmän. Kasvatusalan koulutuksissa on jo runsaasti sisältöjä ja tavoitteita, joihin liikkuminen voidaan luontevasti kiinnittää nykyistä vahvemmin.

title: Five projects awarded funding through Volt – the Nordic culture and language programme for children and young people
content:
The applications covered a wide range of artistic forms including film, literature, photography, sound-art, and poetry. The projects explored the concept of belonging in a variety of ways.

“The highest-scoring projects submitted some robust proposals and took a hands-on approach to exploring what it means to belong,” says Randi Samsonsen, chair of the expert group responsible for funding decisions.

“Another common feature of the projects awarded funding is that they create opportunities for the children and young people involved to meet in person, allowing ideas and experiences to emerge through real-life encounters. For the projects selected, the emphasis is on the quality of interaction, rather than simply the number of participants,” Samsonsen explains.

Nordic Lunch Stories is a youth-led environmental arts project bringing together 12–15-year-olds from Finland, Sweden, and Denmark. Through sound, storytelling, performing arts, and food culture, the young participants collaborate to create an artistic residency, a multilingual soundscape, and a public presentation exploring how we can live more sustainably in our day-to-day lives.

title: A New Search Engine Lets You Explore 4 Million Works of Art & Historical Photographs from Museums and Libraries Around the World
content: We live in an age when you can describe practically anything you want to see in words, then see it almost immediately. Nobody will ever have laid eyes upon that particular sight before — and quite possibly, nobody ever will again. There we have both the upside and the downside of artificial intelligence-powered image generation. A constant flow of visual, aural, or textual novelty offers stimulation, to put it mildly, but it inevitably comes to feel insubstantial. However complexly derived from the work of humanity it may be, it lacks a direct connection to that work. Not so the results delivered by Arkivism, a new search engine that responds to descriptions by drawing on a collection of more than four million pieces of real art and photography.

title: Beware a Balkan Chinese-Russian Cyber Danger
content:
When Bosnia and Herzegovina held general elections last month, it used biometric voter identification and ballot scanners — a reform widely praised for producing fast and accurate results. That’s a real achievement. But the region’s digital foundations remain fragile, and the region’s adversaries know it.

The Balkan chessboard remains checkered, torn between attraction to the European Union and to Russia, with China maneuvering for leverage. Bosnian nationalists, including separatist, pro-Russian Serbs, won the recent vote. But Serbs gave a pro-European student-led movement a clear majority in another October election, while Montenegro and Albania closed chapters in their EU accession talks. 

The cheapest way to shift the balance of power is to undermine trust in the ballot. For the region, cybersecurity is not a technical issue. It is a strategic one. Washington is waking up to the risk — but needs to increase its focus on digital dangers. The EU is already pressing for action but must also increase its scrutiny.

title: Google Summaries Aren't About AI, They're About Lock-In
content:
Whether they call it AI summaries, knowledge panels, or AMP, Google takes actions that are less about functionality and more about locking you into its own ecosystem. Knowing that makes it possible for all of us to choose better services than Google's, defeating their anticompetitive goal. In this case, as it is so often, knowledge is power.  

In the old days, when dinosaurs roamed the earth and getting online involved your computer making eldritch shrieking, Google was a website that took whatever you typed in and gave you a list of links that best matched what you were searching for. As it's grown beyond that, however, the core function of Google Search has moved from giving you the best answer to your query to a number of other things, most of them about making money for Google. 

This is obviously not a new observation. It's at the core of what EFF Special Advisor Cory Doctorow named "enshittification." But it's important to remember that whatever shiny new name or technology is wrapped around these tools, it's not about the wrapping, it's about the monetization.

title: Commission turns to artificial intelligence to write better laws
content:
BRUSSELS — The European Commission is now using artificial intelligence to draft new laws and simplify existing ones, it said in an annual review of progress on its ongoing simplification drive.

As part of a major plan to cut red tape and administrative costs for businesses, the EU is making deep reforms to how it creates and enforces rules on everything from tech, agriculture and migration to environmental protection and taxation.

To do that, the Commission is deploying new digital tools internally to “modernise” lawmaking. The tools aim to help its staff “identify similarities across legal acts, pointing at potential overlaps, inconsistencies or duplicates, as well as opportunities for simplification,” it said in an annual simplification report presented on Wednesday.

According to the document, the Commission is also beefing up legal training and staff to make sure new rules are not overly complex.

title: Thailand: Halt imminent forcible return of two Uyghur men to China
content:
Responding to reports that two Uyghur men recently moved to an Immigration Detention Centre in Thailand face imminent forcible deportation to China, Amnesty International’s Secretary General Agnès Callamard said:

“Thai authorities must immediately halt any plans to forcibly return these two Uyghur men to China, where they face a real risk of torture, arbitrary detention and enforced disappearance. Thailand must not repeat last year’s unlawful deportation of 40 Uyghurs, who were forced back to danger in China.

“These two men fled persecution only to spend more than a decade detained in Thailand. Amnesty International has documented crimes against humanity against Uyghurs and other predominantly Muslim ethnic groups in Xinjiang. Returning them would expose them to the abuses they sought to escape.

“Both men have previously made clear to their legal representatives that they fear for their lives if returned to China and do not consent to being sent back. Thai authorities must now allow them access to a lawyer of their choice and, together with the international community, urgently find a safe and voluntary third-country solution for them and the other Uyghurs still detained in Thailand.

title: "The Earth Shook Last Night": Talarico Wins Senate, Hinojosa Becomes First Latina Governor in Texas
content:
Texas Democrats have shattered more than three decades of Republican dominance in the state, winning races for U.S. Senate, governor, lieutenant governor, attorney general and even railroad commissioner. They are also poised to possibly take control of the Texas House of Representatives for the first time since 2003. The Republican governor of Texas, Greg Abbott, lost his bid for a fourth term to Democratic state Representative Gina Hinojosa, who defeated him by nearly 700,000 votes. She will be Texas’s first Latina governor. And James Talarico will be the first Democrat to represent Texas in the U.S. Senate since 1993.

“We’re celebrating these wonderful candidates who won office, and we’re also starting to think about what it means to hold power,” says Mike Siegel, a city council member from Austin, Texas, who founded Ground Game Texas, a statewide voter turnout organization. “We need to start thinking very quickly about how we will protect public education, how we will stop data centers and the encroachment of AI on our society, how we will protect public schools, how we stop collaboration with ICE.”

title: Tracing the recruitment trap behind Russia’s war
content:
No justice for Bangladeshi workers who are recruited into Russia’s war

Originally published on Global Voices

War-wounded Bangladeshis in Russia plead to return home. Screenshot from a YouTube report by Ekhon TV. Fair use.

Maksudur Rahman was 31 when a labor recruiter arrived in his hometown in Lakshmipur district, southeastern Bangladesh, with a job offer: becoming a janitor in Russia. Nearly every family in the district has someone working overseas, so the pitch landed. According to an international investigation, he borrowed money and paid the broker BDT 1.2 million (about USD 9,800). For a household like his, that is a fortune, but the promised wages made the debt look manageable. He signed up and flew out.

title: COP31: Human Rights Critical for Climate Action
content:
(Istanbul) – Governments participating in the 31st annual United Nations climate change conference (COP31) should urgently act to protect the rights of communities displaced by the climate crisis and ensure that civil society groups can participate in the negotiations, Human Rights Watch said today. 

COP31 will take place in Antalya, Türkiye, from November 9 to 20, 2026, under the shared presidency of Türkiye and Australia, on behalf of the Pacific Region. Negotiating countries and international climate funds should ensure that the needs of communities on the front lines of climate impacts and fencelines of fossil fuel extraction are driving the discussions, not corporate interests. 

“Intensifying climate impacts are already uprooting entire communities, yet those bearing these consequences are too often excluded from the decisions that determine their futures,” said Maria Laura Canineu, deputy environment director at Human Rights Watch. “Governments in Antalya should put affected communities at the center of climate action by ensuring that adaptation finance flows to displaced communities and to defending the space for civil society to hold government leaders accountable.”

title: What do Taylor Swift and Giorgia Meloni have in common?
content: Taylor Swift, a billionaire pop empress, and Giorgia Meloni, the far-right Italian prime minister, aren't often mentioned in the same breath. But they're caught in a similar battle, both trying to find new ways to fight an army of AI deepfakes by filing for EU trademarks to protect their voices. Swift's company, TAS Rights Management LLC, wants to register her saying “Hey, it's Taylor Swift”, according to a 6 October filing at the EU Intellectual Property Office. Meloni filed on 5 October to register herself saying “Io sono Giorgia Meloni.” While you can't trademark someone's voice as a whole, these trademarks would give them the exclusive right to their voice saying those words. That could technically stop anyone else from using the voice for a deepfake. Infringing a trademark risks lawsuits and claims for financial damage. It might also be easier to get tech platforms to quickly remove trademark-infringing content. Swift already filed for a US trademark for her voice earlier this year. title: ‘There Is One Fight’: American Voters Reject Tech Oligarchy
content:
Last month, OpenAI CEO Sam Altman told Politico that “we believe that the world should accept some bad things happening for the benefits of this technology,” referring to ChatGPT users dying, people losing their jobs to AI, and the other negative externalities we have seen from AI. 

Altman wasn’t running for office Tuesday. But this worldview—that the masses must shut up and suffer while oligarchs centralize power, self-deal, spend wildly to capture the political process, and automate away human endeavors so they can amass yet more wealth—was wholly repudiated in Tuesday’s election as people in Red States, Blue States, and Purple States rejected the cruelty, corruption, and depravity economy we’ve seen over the last few years. They are tired of kleptocracy.

title: US Sentences Venezuelan National to 12 Years for Laundering Over $1 Billion
content:
A U.S. district court sentenced a 60-year-old Venezuelan national Jorge Figueira to 12 years in prison and ordered him to surrender $1 billion for running a money laundering network tied to drug trafficking organizations, according to a Tuesday statement.

Investigators found that Figueira's operation moved over $1 billion through a single cryptocurrency wallet and various financial accounts. The network funneled the illicit funds into and out of the U.S. using shell companies, traditional bank accounts, and cryptocurrency exchanges, directing outbound money to individuals and businesses worldwide, including in Colombia, China, Panama, and Mexico.

title: Vermont Has Spent Nearly a Billion Dollars to Clean Up Lake Champlain. But the Green Slime Keeps Coming Back.
content:
On the last day of August, Jeff van den Noort spotted thick swirls of neon green film coating the water just steps from his home in Vermont. He waded in up to his ankles and dipped a jar to get a sample of the scum.

It wasn’t the first time he’d seen the slime. Since his parents bought the house on an island in Lake Champlain in 1966, van den Noort has spent part of nearly every summer in this quiet spot. Back then, the lake was clear.

But he began to witness the water’s deterioration as he grew older, especially after he moved into the home full time in 2010 to care for his ailing mother. That day in late August was the worst he’d seen all summer. 

Later that week, van den Noort grabbed a bucket, a few Mason jars and a smartphone and got into his rusty Saab. He drove past the boat launches, frozen-in-time general stores and windswept pastures of the lake’s islands in northern Vermont and stopped at four other spots along the shore. Each time, he collected some murky water, gauged how thick the muck was, took a few photos and jotted down the weather conditions. He then uploaded his report to an online database.

title: Speaking in a second language may shift your moral compass – but it can’t overpower it
content:
In today’s interconnected world, millions of people move between two or more languages every day. They may negotiate at work in one language, speak with family in another, and follow news, entertainment and social media across several others.

Using multiple languages can deeply change the way a person sees the world. Research has suggested that thinking and speaking in different languages can fundamentally shift the way we reason and behave, and even change our morality.

Some studies have suggested that using a second language encourages people to make more rational, utilitarian choices, meaning they prioritise the greatest good for the greatest number of people. This is possibly because moral dilemmas feel less emotionally charged when processed in a second language.

But the effect is not cut and dried – other studies have found little or no such effect.

One reason for these mixed findings is that language is only one part of the story. People do not enter a dilemma as a blank slate – they also bring values, past experiences, and sense of self. To date, most research has focused primarily on which language people use, while paying less attention to the person making the decision.

title: Climate change is undermining our health and the burden falls heaviest on women
content:
As sea levels creep higher in the Pacific, salt leaches into the soil, and reduces the land available to grow food. Ocean warming is damaging coral reefs, reducing fish stocks, and salinity has tainted fresh water supplies.

As a result, Pacific communities are being forced to turn to imported food, which is often high in calories but low in nutrients. And this, along with a myriad of intersecting social, cultural, and economic factors, has led to a rise in the rates of chronic diseases, such as diabetes and cardiovascular disease.

Ahead of the upcoming UN climate conference COP31, discussions by government ministers, civil society advocates, multilateral agencies, and academics at the pre-COP meeting in Fiji and Tuvalu last month emphasised the importance of health for those on the front line of the climate crisis.

Women in the Pacific are disproportionately responsible for family care, and the burden of food and water insecurity falls most heavily on their shoulders. Women at the pre-COP meeting told us replanting crops after extreme weather is increasing their domestic burden, contributing to exhaustion and mental ill-health.

title: Yhdysvaltain välivaalit antavat toivoa, myös ilmastolle
content:
Yhdysvaltain välivaalit antavat maailmalle jotakin, mistä on viime aikoina ollut puutetta: toivoa. Demokraatit voittivat sekä edustajainhuonee että senaatin, ja tulos on selvä tappio presidentti Donald Trumpin johtamalle republikaanipuolueelle.

Trump onnitteli demokraatteja ja ilmoitti olevansa valmis yhteistyöhön. Samalla hän uhkasi käyttää veto-oikeuttaan demokraattien lakiesityksiä vastaan pakottaakseen nämä neuvottelupöytään. Kongressin enemmistön vaihtuminen vaikeuttaa joka tapauksessa Trumpin mahdollisuuksia toteuttaa politiikkaansa presidenttikauden jäljellä olevina kahtena vuotena.

Äänestäjät ovat vaihtaneet suuntaa muuallakin. Puolassa kansallismielinen Laki ja oikeus -puolue oli vallassa kahdeksan vuotta mutta menetti vuoden 2023 vaaleissa enemmistönsä, vaikka sen hallitsema valtiollinen televisio väitti vielä kaksi päivää vaalien jälkeen puolueen voittaneen. Unkarissa Viktor Orbánin 16 vuotta jatkunut valtakausi päättyi tänä keväänä opposition vaalivoittoon. Molemmissa maissa vallanpitäjät olivat pyrkineet vahvistamaan asemaansa myös median ja yhteiskunnallisten instituutioiden kautta. Siitä huolimatta oppositio onnistui voittamaan vaalit.

title: Q&A: What is in the global ‘roadmap’ for transitioning away from fossil fuels?
content:
• Why has Brazil produced a fossil-fuel ‘roadmap’?
  • What does the fossil-fuel roadmap say?
  • How will the fossil-fuel roadmap be discussed at COP31?

    • Transitioning away from fossil fuels is “urgent, inevitable and, yet, possible”, according to a first-of-its-kind global “roadmap” produced by Brazil.

    The host of last year’s climate summit, COP30, has set out a voluntary plan for how countries can move away from coal, oil and gas.

    The roadmap says there is no “one-size-fits-all” approach to transitioning away from fossil fuels and asks countries to “diagnose” their own “readiness” to start the process.

    After mapping out their specific circumstances, countries should then pursue “tailored levers” to take action, according to the roadmap.

    These efforts should culminate by 2033, it says – 10 years on from when the COP28 climate summit in Dubai called on all countries to contribute to a global transition away from fossil fuels.

    Below, Carbon Brief examines what the roadmap says and how it could influence debates about fossil fuels at the upcoming COP31 climate summit, which begins next week in Turkey.

title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time review – a dream come true
content:
Nintendo Switch 2; Nintendo
This ambitious remake transforms a landmark Zelda game into a modern masterpiece, clearer and easier to navigate, more beautiful to look at, with playful musical touches. Yet the melancholy remains

It’s always a worry, returning to a formative piece of art from your childhood. Will your jaded adult sensibilities render you unable to locate the magic that captivated your child self? Will revisiting it reveal that it was never actually that good, and that your tastes are built on a foundation of lies? With video games, there is the added complication of technological advancement: decades-old games can look so basic and feel so treacly to play that it’s hard to explain why they were mind-blowing at the time.

Light-touch remasters aim to bring such games up to modern graphical standards without fundamentally changing them; an ambitious remake attempts to transform the work into something that can stand alongside any modern masterpiece. Ocarina of Time is the latter. And I could not be more delighted to report that it is a dream come true.

title: Abdul El-Sayed Becomes First Muslim Senator as Democrats Rout GOP Across the U.S. in Rebuke to Trump
content:
In a stunning repudiation of President Trump, Democrats regained control of both chambers of Congress in Tuesday’s midterm elections, flipping seven Senate seats: Iowa, Kansas, Ohio, Maine, North Carolina and South Carolina. Meanwhile, progressive Democrat Dr. Abdul El-Sayed defeated former Republican Congressmember Mike Rogers for an open Senate seat in Michigan with over 52% of the vote. El-Sayed campaigned on a platform of Medicare for All, tackling economic inequality and getting big money out of politics — as well as ending military aid to Israel. He is the first Muslim elected to the U.S. Senate. El-Sayed faced vitriolic, Islamaphobic attacks by top Republicans throughout the campaign.

“Last night wasn’t just about Dr. Abdulrahman being a Muslim, winning and going to the United States Senate,” says Palestinian American organizer and author Linda Sarsour, who has been campaigning for El-Sayed. “It demonstrated that progressives can win in states like Michigan” and that “we can win on standing up for the human rights of the Palestinian people.”

title: Burkina Faso: Islamist Armed Group Targets Civilians
content:
(Nairobi) – An Al-Qaeda-linked armed group killed at least 27 civilians in two attacks in Burkina Faso’s northern Yatenga province in September 2026, Human Rights Watch said today. These attacks violated international humanitarian law and are apparent war crimes.

On September 1, the Group for the Support of Islam and Muslims (Jama’at Nusrat al-Islam wal-Muslimin, or JNIM) attacked a gold mining site in Soubo, Ouahigouya district, killing 24 civilians, injuring at least 20 others, and burning property. On September 5, three civilians on a motorcycle, including a child, were killed by an explosive weapon on a dirt track near Mera village, also in Ouahigouya district. Local residents believe JNIM forces had planted an improvised explosive device (IED).

“The JNIM armed group’s relentless, unlawful attacks put civilians across Burkina Faso at grave risk,” said Ilaria Allegrozzi, senior Sahel researcher at Human Rights Watch. “The authorities should urgently strengthen protection for threatened communities, investigate abuses, and fairly prosecute those responsible.”

title: Funding to help poorer countries cope with climate crisis has stalled, says UN
content:
Report reveals financial support promised by rich nations for adaptation measures is well behind the pace that is needed

Flows of money to help poor countries cope with the climate crisis have been flat or falling since 2022, despite growing impacts from extreme weather and warnings from scientists that global heating may be accelerating.

A new UN report has revealed that financial support for adaptation – which includes measures such as stronger infrastructure, early warning systems, flood protection and drought-resilient irrigation – is woefully short of what is needed and far behind even the inadequate promises that rich countries signed up to in 2021 in recognition of their far greater responsibility for the crisis.

title: Domestic abuse leaves receipts
content: Your bank statement says a lot about your lifestyle. For women, it could also provide early hints of domestic abuse, according to a recent Nature paper. Using data from Lloyds, the UK's largest retail bank, the study found certain banking patterns in domestic abuse victims' statements as early as seven years before they disclosed their situation. The authors compared more than 5,000 women who had told their bank they were experiencing abuse with over 15,600 customers who had not. Women who disclosed abuse were more likely to have missed a payment, and had lower credit scores. They were also more likely to receive welfare benefits, and their savings were £3,500 lower on average. Their spending patterns also differed: they spent less on self-care, such as the dentist, optician, or sports, and more on alcohol – possibly as a coping strategy, the authors noted. They also spent more on taxis and legal fees. They withdrew cash and changed PIN numbers and address more often, which the authors argue could hint at an abuser taking control of their finances, but also victims regaining it after leaving. title: Donald Trump Jr. Discussed Deals With Russian Businessman Close to Putin’s Personal Security Chief, Two Sources Say
content:
Donald Trump Jr. makes no secret of his relationship with Kremlin-linked businessman Umar Kremlev.

In 2025, the two men appeared together on stage in Istanbul at a meeting of the International Boxing Association, of which Kremlev is president. “I am proud to call Umar not only a leader but a friend,” Trump Jr. said.

And earlier this year, after ProPublica revealed that Kremlev had rented out a private island for Trump Jr.’s wedding, his new wife posted on Instagram that this had been “an extraordinarily generous” gift from “our dear friend Umar.”

But now, as reported by OCCRP’s Russian partner Important Stories, there may be more than friendship on the agenda. Two sources independently told the outlet’s reporters that Kremlev told them he and Trump Jr. had met in Kazakhstan to discuss business deals earlier this year.

Kremlev referred to those encounters as “business meetings,” they said. Both sources were quoted anonymously to ensure their safety.

title: Do You Live Near Lake Champlain? Help Seven Days and ProPublica Investigate Algae Blooms.
content:
Despite being an iconic part of Vermont’s landscape and a large source of the state’s drinking water, Lake Champlain has been polluted for decades. Phosphorus runoff from farm fields, rural roads, parking lots, stormwater drains and wastewater treatment plants flows into the lake, fueling algae blooms that frequently choke its bays and shorelines.

Vermont is halfway through a 20-year effort to clean up the lake. In 2016, the U.S. Environmental Protection Agency established new, stricter requirements for reducing phosphorus runoff that the state must meet by 2036. But more than a decade in, after spending nearly a billion dollars, the state is lagging behind. Water quality has not improved dramatically, and in some parts of the lake, it is getting worse. This past summer algae blooms shut down swimming at public beaches in St. Albans Bay in the northeast part of the lake.

title: Donald Trump’s Republicans suffer landslide defeat – what this means for the world
content:
Donald Trump’s Republican Party has received a stunning rebuke in the US midterm elections. Republicans went into the evening hoping that the polls might be wrong and that they could at least cling on to control of the Senate. But by midnight in Washington, the GOP was staring down what looked like its worst defeat in 50 years.

Republican losses were not just confined to the type of swing districts that parties usually worry about on election night. The scale of the losses was staggering. They lost Senate seats in deep red states such as Texas and South Carolina. They lost districts they had gerrymandered and in which they were supposed to be unbeatable. They lost seats that even the sharpest analysts thought were safe.

Why? For months, surveys have shown that voters are fed up with high prices, with the war in Iran, and with what is increasingly being talked about as the Trump administration’s corruption. A president who was narrowly elected on the promise of a steady economic hand instead spent two years pursuing an extreme ideological agenda favoured only by a minority of Americans. He ignored what voters were saying, and now they have delivered a harsh verdict.

title: Agatha Christie: A World of Mystery is a brilliant exploration of the life of the queen of crime
content:
Coinciding with the 50th anniversary of Agatha Christie’s death, the exhibition A World of Mystery at the British Library takes visitors on a fascinating journey through spaces that evoke Christie’s life and work. This landmark exhibition offers unprecedented access to a body of private papers, diaries, manuscripts and family objects, brought together for public view for the first time.

Beautifully curated by Lucy Rowland, there is an impressive array of artefacts celebrating Christie’s life and work. Visitors can see objects that conjure important moments in Christie’s life from her Devon childhood to her travels around the globe, and her enormously successful career as novelist and playwright.

title: CB Live: Carbon Brief’s team at COP17 on the nature talks’ key outcomes
content:
Following this year’s UN COP17 biodiversity conference, Carbon Brief’s journalists hosted a livestream to explain what happened at the summit.

Carbon Brief’s Orla Dwyer and Aruna Chandrasekhar have been on the ground in Yerevan, Armenia, over the past two weeks, covering the negotiations.

They were joined on the livestream by associate editors Dr Giuliana Viglione and Daisy Dunne, who were following the talks from Washington DC and London, respectively.

Carbon Brief has also published its 10,000-word explainer of COP17, which lays out the key outcomes in detail.

Membership

Orla and Aruna kicked off the livestream by explaining the biggest issues at the event, including biodiversity finance and the first “global review” of progress towards reversing nature loss.

The four journalists then took live questions from the audience in an “ask me anything” format, covering issues such as “nature-harming subsidies”, marine biodiversity and the status of the Cali fund, which is meant to raise private-sector finance.

A recording of the webinar (below) is now available to watch on YouTube.

title: Bangladesh: Academics Allegedly Targeted for Supporting Hasina
content:
(London) – Scores of academics and students at public universities in Bangladesh have been arbitrarily punished because of their alleged affiliation with former ruler Sheikh Hasina and her Awami League party, Human Rights Watch said today.

Any action to punish persons for their peaceful beliefs or without ensuring due process would violate the rights to freedom of expression and association protected under international human rights law and reproduce abusive attempts under previous administrations to control political opinion and expression at Bangladesh’s public universities.

“Bangladesh has a long history of political debate in its universities, and only autocrats should fear such discourse, not a government formed following student protests,” said Meenakshi Ganguly, deputy Asia director at Human Rights Watch. “Bangladesh needs to turn the page on the repression of the past, not repeat it whenever the ruling and opposition parties trade places.”

title: Rioting for a reason
content: If you've glanced at the news lately, you've probably seen many reports about riots, looting, and violence at protests across Europe. These protests are driven mostly by young people demanding better school conditions and affordable housing, among other things. Yet many headlines focus on violence or riots rather than protestors' demands. Of the more than 10,000 news reports of protests in France by European outlets, just 8% of headlines explicitly mentioned protest demands. Meanwhile, around one in three headlines mentioned terms related to violence. In fact, some of the most-used words in headlines are associated with violence, including “riot”, “clash”, “chaos”, and “violence” itself.

title: We used ancient DNA to track the origins and spread of the Germanic and Celtic languages – new research
content:
Why do people speak Germanic languages such as English in England and Swedish in Sweden, but Celtic languages in Ireland, Wales and Brittany? The dispersal of languages is one of the enigmas of European prehistory.

Two new studies in Nature, which we took part in, show how DNA from several thousand ancient individuals helps us solve this riddle.

As early as the 17th century, scholars noticed striking similarities between the European languages. English father, Swedish fader, Irish athair, Latin pater and Greek patḗr do not resemble each other by coincidence. Today, we know that these languages, together with Baltic, Slavic, Indic and Iranian, evolved from a common ancestor: Proto-Indo-European.

But how did this ancestral language come to be spoken so widely across Eurasia? During the 19th and 20th centuries, a wide variety of theories were developed about its origin. One of these placed its homeland on the vast grassy steppes north of the Black and Caspian Seas around 5,000 years ago.

Subsequent migrations by the pastoral nomads of the Yamnaya culture are thought to have spread the ancestral language across Europe and Asia.

title: Thailand: Two Uyghurs at Risk of Return to China
content:
(Bangkok) – Thai authorities should not forcibly return two Uyghur men to China, where they face grave risks of torture and other serious abuses, Human Rights Watch said today. The two men, whose names are not public for security reasons, were transferred from prison to immigration detention in Bangkok after receiving a royal pardon, apparently in preparation for deportation.

“Previous Thai governments have kept Uyghurs in inhumane detention for years and then complied with Beijing’s demands to send them to China, where they were forcibly disappeared,” said Elaine Pearson, Asia director at Human Rights Watch. “Thai Prime Minister Anutin Charnvirakul should end forced returns to China and allow the two Uyghur men to travel to a safe third country.”

title: Why Trump, Xi, and Putin can’t carve up the world like the ‘big three’ leaders of 1945
content:
Discussions are underway for a potential meeting between Donald Trump, Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin on the margins of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit on November 18-19. The prospect has prompted comparisons with the “Big Three” summit in Yalta in February 1945 at which the leaders of Britain, the US and the Soviet Union discussed a carve up of the world following the second world war.

It is clear that Trump, Xi and Putin, each in charge of a country that considers itself a “great power”, rather like the idea of a new world order that will revolve around them. The US president appears to see himself as one of a modern triumvirate with presidents Putin and Xi who – like their 1945 predecessors – can propose and dispose of other nations as they please.

For these leaders alone, Trump appears to show respect and deference – compared to the disdain he demonstrates for most others presidents and prime ministers.

title: Who gets to call the water “safe” – Spilling the Truth Workshop (7 October 2026)
content:
by Jakleen Al-Dalal’a

For someone checking a storm overflow map before a swim, the question may seem straightforward: is it safe to enter the water? In our online workshop, participants questioned what a “safe” label would mean for people swimming, paddling or working beside a river. Their discussion raised a further question about the advice a map might offer: what would readers need to know before deciding whether it applied to their own activity and circumstances?

title: Sosiaalihuollon uusi asiakastietojärjestelmä otetaan käyttöön 17.11.2026 – muutos voi aiheuttaa viivettä palveluihin
content:
Pohjois-Karjalan hyvinvointialue – Siun sote aloittaa uuden asiakas- potilastietojärjestelmän käyttöönoton. Ensimmäisenä käyttöön otetaan sosiaalihuollon asiakastietojärjestelmä tiistaina 17.11.2026. Uuteen asiakastietojärjestelmään siirtyvät ensimmäisessä vaiheessa perhepalvelut, työikäisten palvelut, vammaispalvelut ja osa iäkkäiden palveluista.

Sosiaalihuollon asiakastietojärjestelmän käyttöönotto on osa Siun soten laajaa asiakas- ja potilastietojärjestelmäuudistusta, jossa hyvinvointialue siirtyy vaiheittain käyttämään yhteistä Lifecare-järjestelmää sosiaali- ja terveyspalveluissa.

Uudistus toteutetaan vaiheittain. Sosiaalipalvelujen jälkeen uuden järjestelmän käyttöön siirtyvät suunterveydenhuolto, perusterveydenhuolto, kotihoito, erikoissairaanhoito sekä muut sosiaali- ja terveydenhuollon palvelut. Koko uudistuksen on tarkoitus valmistua vuoden 2027 loppuun mennessä.

Asiakastietojärjestelmän käyttöönotto vaikuttaa väliaikaisesti sosiaalihuollon palveluihin. Käyttöönoton jälkeisinä viikkoina palveluissa voi esiintyä

title: Suomalaisten tiedelehtien toimitustyö
content: Tieteellisten lehtien toimitustyö on keskeinen, mutta verraten vähän tutkittu osa akateemista julkaisujärjestelmää erityisesti kansallisissa, avoimesti julkaisevissa tiedelehdissä. Tässä artikkelissa tarkastellaan suomalaisten tieteellisten lehtien toimitustyötä organisoinnin, laadunvarmistuksen sekä kehittämisen ja toiminnan jatkuvuuden näkökulmista. Tutkimus perustuu Webropol-kyselyaineistoon, joka kerättiin alkuvuonna 2026 ja johon vastasi 94 toimitusten edustajaa 87 suomalaisesta tiedelehdestä. Aineisto analysoitiin yhdistämällä kuvailevaa tilastollista tarkastelua ja laadullista sisällönanalyysiä. Tulokset osoittavat, että suomalaisten tiedelehtien toimitustyö nojaa vahvasti pienten toimituskuntien vapaaehtoistyöhön ja niukkoihin resursseihin. Toimitustyön organisointi rakentuu vakiintuneiden mutta joustavien roolien varaan, joissa vastuu kasautuu usein päätoimittajille ja toimitussihteereille. Laadunvarmistus toteutuu pääosin luotettavien vertaisarviointikäytäntöjen, kollegiaalisen tuen ja yksittäisten toimittajien asiantuntijuuden kautta, mutta eettisten kysymysten systemaattinen käsittely ja dokumentointi ovat paikoin puutteellisia. Kehittämistyötä ja toiminnan jatkuvuuden turvaamista vaikeuttavat erityisesti ajan ja rahoituksen puute, vaikka toimituksissa tunnistetaan tarve kouluttautumiselle, dokumentaation vahvistamiselle ja osaamisen siirtämiselle. Artikkeli tuo näkyväksi kotimaisen tiedejulkaisemisen rakenteellisen haavoittuvuuden ja korostaa tarvetta vahvistaa toimitustyön institutionaalista tunnustamista ja kestävää resursointia.

title: Tutkimus: Icehearts vähentää nuorisorikollisuutta myös lähiympäristössä
content:
Tuoreen rekisteritutkimuksen mukaan rikoksesta epäiltyinä poliisirekisteriin päätyneiden alle 16-vuotiaiden osuus väheni Icehearts-toiminnan kohdealueilla kaksi prosenttiyksikköä eli 18 prosenttia lähtötasosta. Tutkimuksessa havaittiin myös viitteitä kouluarvosanojen paranemisesta, ja myönteiset vaikutukset ulottuivat toimintaan suoraan osallistumattomiin lapsiin ja nuoriin. Tulokset vahvistavat aiempaa näyttöä Icehearts-toiminnan vaikuttavuudesta. Aiemmassa kustannusvaikuttavuustutkimuksessa yhden kasvattajan ja noin 20 lapsen joukkueen 12-vuotisen toiminnan laskennalliseksi yhteiskunnalliseksi nettosäästöksi arvioitiin vähintään 2,8 miljoonaa euroa.

Aalto-yliopiston taloustieteen väitöskirjatutkija Ellen Sahlströmin tutkimuksessa tarkastellaan Iceheartsin tarjoaman pitkäjänteisen tuen vaikutuksia toiminnassa mukana oleviin poikiin sekä tuen heijastevaikutuksia alueen muihin samanikäisiin lapsiin ja nuoriin. Icehearts-toiminnassa on myös tyttöjen joukkueita, mutta toimintaan osallistuneita koskeva tutkimusasetelma rajautui tässä tutkimuksessa poikiin.

title: Creative Europe opens 2027 call for literary translation and promotion
content:
The call ‘circulation of European literary works’ supports the translation, publication, distribution and promotion of European literature, including novels, poetry, comics and plays, with a focus on works written in less widely translated languages.

Promoting reading and helping readers discover the diversity of languages and cultures reflected in European literature are also key objectives.

Publishers, booksellers and libraries are encouraged to work together to strengthen the book sector’s competitiveness. Ensuring fair pay and good working conditions for literary translators is also a priority.

Organisations in the publishing and book sector based in an eligible country can apply individually or as a group of two or more partners.

Each project must include a minimum of five eligible literary works, supported by a strong publishing strategy and a distribution plan.

The authors must be nationals or residents of an eligible country or be recognised as part of Europe’s literary heritage.

An online information session will take place on 17 November 2026 from 14:00 to 16:00.

title: Pohjois-Karjala näyttää suuntaa – kulttuurihyvinvoinnista osa suomalaista hyvinvointipolitiikkaa
content:
Miten kulttuurin hyvinvointivaikutukset saadaan nykyistä vahvemmin osaksi suomalaista hyvinvoinnin ja terveyden edistämistä? Pohjois-Karjalassa on kehitetty maakunnallista yhteistyötä, jossa kulttuuripalvelut, sosiaali- ja terveydenhuolto sekä kulttuurialan toimijat tuodaan lähemmäksi toisiaan. 

Suomen sosiaali- ja terveydenhuollossa etsitään ratkaisuja kasvaviin kustannuksiin, väestön ikääntymiseen ja palvelujen saatavuuteen. Samalla korostuu tarve vahvistaa hyvinvointia ennaltaehkäisevästi. Taiteen ja kulttuurin mahdollisuudet ovat tässä keskustelussa edelleen osittain hyödyntämättä.

Taiteella ja kulttuurilla on monenlaisia myönteisiä yhteyksiä terveyteen ja hyvinvointiin. Tutkimuksissa on havaittu vaikutuksia muun muassa mielenterveyteen, sosiaaliseen osallisuuteen sekä sairauksien ehkäisyyn ja hoidon tukemiseen. Kulttuuritoiminta voi siten täydentää sosiaali- ja terveyspalveluja ja tarjota uusia mahdollisuuksia hyvinvoinnin edistämiseen.

title: Viisi hanketta sai tukea nuorten kulttuuri- ja kieliohjelma Voltista
content:
Hankehakemukset edustivat elokuvan, kirjallisuuden ja valokuvauksen kaltaisia ilmaisumuotoja sekä äänitaidetta ja runoutta. Hankkeet lähestyivät yhteenkuuluvuuden tunnetta monesta näkökulmasta.

– Korkeat pisteet saaneilla hankkeilla oli hyvin konkreettiset hakemukset ja käytännönläheinen tapa lähestyä yhteenkuuluvuutta, sanoo hankepäätöksistä vastaavan asiantuntijaryhmän puheenjohtaja Randi Samsonsen.

– Tuettujen hankkeiden yhteisenä kriteerinä oli myös se, että hankkeeseen osallistuvat lapset ja nuoret kohtaavat toisensa tosielämässä. Asioiden on toisin sanoen voitava kehittyä todellisten kohtaamisten kautta. Tuetuissa hankkeissa yhteenkuuluvuutta tarkasteltiin laadullisesta eikä vain määrällisestä näkökulmasta, Samsonsen selittää.

Nordic Lunch Stories on nuorten vetämä ympäristöaiheinen taideprojekti, joka tuo yhteen 12–15-vuotiaita nuoria Suomesta, Ruotsista ja Tanskasta. Nuoret luovat äänten, tarinankerronnan, esittävän taiteen ja ruokakulttuurin avulla yhdessä taiteilijaresidenssin, monikielisen äänimaiseman sekä julkisen esityksen siitä, miten arjessa voidaan elää kestävästi.

title: Föreslå din favorit till Årets museum 2027
content:
Vilket museum inspirerar, överraskar och gör skillnad? Nu söker Sveriges Museer och Svenska ICOM kandidater till Årets museum 2027. Vem som helst kan vara med och påverka genom att föreslå ett museum som förtjänar att uppmärksammas för sitt arbete.

Varje år tilldelas ett svenskt museum utmärkelsen Årets museum för att ha visat prov på mod, kreativitet och spets. Priset lyfter fram museer som vågar tänka nytt, utvecklar sin verksamhet och stärker museernas roll i samhället.

Syftet är att uppmärksamma framstående museiarbete och inspirera till nytänkande verksamhet av högsta kvalitet. År 2027 delas utmärkelsen ut för 31 gången. Bakom priset står Sveriges Museer och Svenska ICOM.

Alla kan föreslå ett museum – stort som litet, från hela landet. De inkomna förslagen ligger sedan till grund för juryns arbete med att utse tre finalister.

Föreslå ditt favoritmuseum här>>

Årets museum ska uppvisa mod, kreativitet och spets inom ett eller flera av följande områden:

Relevans: Årets museum utgör en angelägen och inkluderande arena för människor och samhället.

Inspiration: Årets museum kan uppvisa framstående exempel på nyskapande och innovativ verksamhet inom något eller flera områden.

title: Suomi110-juhlavuoteen sopivia ohjelmia etsitään
content:
Opetus- ja kulttuuriministeriö kokoaa tapahtumakalenteria juhlavuoden aikana toteutuvasta taiteesta ja kulttuurista. Ilmoittakaa tapahtumanne, näyttelynne ja muut sopivat ohjelmat osaksi Suomi110-juhlintaa!

Opetus- ja kulttuuriministeriö järjestää 110 vuotta täyttävän itsenäisen Suomen kunniaksi yhteistyökumppaneidensa kanssa 28. helmikuuta 2027 juhlatilaisuuden. Tarkoituksena on lisäksi koota tapahtumakalenteri juhlavuoden aikana toteutuvasta taiteesta ja kulttuurista. Kalenteri julkaistaan vuoden 2027 alussa.

Kalenteria varten opetus- ja kulttuuriministeriölle voi toimittaa tiedot sellaisista tapahtumista, näyttelyistä tai muista ohjelmistoista, jotka edustavat suomalaista kulttuuria, kulttuuriperintöä tai taidetta. Näiden tulee olla alkuperäisiä suomalaisia teoksia, kuten näytelmiä tai sävellyksiä, suomalaisten taiteilijoiden näyttelyitä tai suomalaista kulttuuriperintöä käsitteleviä ohjelmistoja. Kokonaisuuksien tulee olla juhlavuoden (2027) puolella. Juhlavuoteen voivat osallistua niin valtakunnalliset tapahtumat kuin paikalliset yhteisötilaisuudet.

title: The San Francisco Public Library Launches a Free Online Archive with 80,000+ Historical Images & Documents to Explore & Download
content: Over 100,000 people move to the San Francisco Bay Area each year. Their motivations for doing so no doubt vary, but these days, the ambition to make a fortune at the epicenter of the tech industry — especially amid the rapidly inflating AI bubble — is hardly unheard of. Unfortunately, that desire can be so all-consuming as to crowd out any interest in, or even curiosity about, the city itself, to say nothing of its wider region. Yet the San Francisco we know today is the result of a story at least 250 years long, very little of which has much to do with venture capital or GPUs. Now, anyone who does want to make a start on understanding it can do so at the new-and-improved platform DigitalSF, with its more than 80,000 historical items available to view and download.

title: Canada’s “Associate” EU Membership Should Be Digital
content:
When European Union leaders traveled to Montreal this month for the EU-Canada summit, they launched a grandly named “Alliance for the Future,” proposing to make Canada an “associate member” of the EU. A key part of the plan should be digital.

Europe has already negotiated five Digital Partnerships with like-minded democratic countries. Japan was the first, inking a digital deal in 2022. Since then, the EU has established agreements with South Korea, Singapore, Brazil, and Canada. 

In Montreal, Canada and the EU agreed on a legal framework to protect data flows from localization barriers and decided that Canada could participate in the EU’s high-performance computing partnership. But the existing digital partnerships remain, fundamentally, non-binding talk shops.

The motivation behind strengthening the deals is clear: reduce reliance on the US and China. But reinforced digital partnerships with like-minded democracies must push back against strong protectionist instincts, while remaining open to new participants, including the US — perhaps through a revived transatlantic Trade and Technology Council.

title: Postal Service Surveilled Protest Activities Online With Little Rules, Oversight
content:
The U.S. Postal Service used social media surveillance to monitor and report on protests across the political spectrum, government records show.

The records, disclosed to EFF and other requesters suing the postal service under the Freedom of Information Act, show that the agency’s internet Covert Operations Program, or iCOP, routinely sifted through social media posts organizing and discussing protests with little records of any oversight or legal justification.

EFF filed suit in 2021 after Yahoo News disclosed the program’s existence and how the agency used it to monitor First Amendment protected activities. After years of delays and technical failures that led the agency to lose access to a trove of emails discussing the program, the postal service disclosed records to EFF and several other requesters this year.

title: The Cloud and AI Development Act Proposal
content:
Throughout the EU, there is a clear political ambition to use public procurement as a lever to reduce reliance on a small number of non-EU cloud service providers and to open the market to a wider range of providers. The Commission presents its proposal for a Cloud and AI Development Act (CADA) as a way to ‘decrease overreliance on certain providers’. Yet, as the CADA proposal is designed, it is more likely to preserve the status quo than to enable public procurement to be used to scale up an open source and interoperable European digital stack.

title: Brussels sets slimline legislative agenda for 2027
content:
BRUSSELS — The European Commission is scaling back its legislative ambitions for 2027, prioritizing competitiveness, deregulation and economic security as the clock starts to run down on Ursula von der Leyen’s second term. 

According to its annual Work Programme and related annexes obtained by POLITICO, the EU wants to strengthen the single market, cut red tape, modernize industry and bolster its defense capabilities at a time of mounting geopolitical risks and economic uncertainty. 

The Commission released the final version of the program and annexes on Wednesday.

“The EU must retain the ability to forge its own path,” the Commission says, adding that “independence is our priority for Europe’s economy.” 

But with existing initiatives — such as the Industrial Accelerator Act — facing delays, Brussels is focusing on getting legislation that is already in preparation across the finish line. 

It’s also killing off proposals that have no chance of passing, along with a crop of outdated regulations — including one on sales of butter stocks to the long-defunct Soviet Union.

title: Peru: Closing the investigation into forced sterilisations perpetuates impunity
content:
Amnesty International condemns the decision by Peru’s Public Prosecutor’s Office to close the investigation into the forced sterilisation of 4,172 Peruvian women during the 1990s. This decision was taken pursuant to Law 32107, passed in 2024, which allows statutes of limitations to be applied to war crimes and crimes against humanity committed before 1 July 2002.

“Closing an investigation that the Public Prosecutor’s Office itself recognises as involving crimes against humanity is an affront to the victims, who have waited almost 30 years for justice. The Peruvian state cannot use a law that contravenes international law to block their path to truth, justice and reparation. This decision must be reversed and Law 32107 repealed to prevent it from continuing to be used as a tool of impunity,” said Ana Piquer, Americas Director at Amnesty International.

Closing an investigation that the Public Prosecutor’s Office itself recognises as involving crimes against humanity is an affront to the victims, who have waited almost 30 years for justice.”

title: Latino Voters Swing Away from Trump for "Terrorizing Our Communities": Marisa Franco of Mijente
content:
In 2024, Donald Trump won the presidency with the support of 44% of Hispanic voters, suggesting that a major realignment in party preferences might be underway. But just two years later, it appears much of that support has eroded. Sixty-one percent of Hispanic voters say they will now support Democrats in the midterms, including 11% who previously had voted for President Trump.

We get a bird’s-eye view of what to expect from the Latino vote from Marisa Franco, the co-founder and director of the advocacy organization Mijente. While ICE brutality will be at the front of voters’ minds, she says, Democrats cannot continue to take Latino voters for granted. “The vast majority of Latinos are working-class. Quite simply, they voted for Trump because they were looking at issues of economy, cost, inflation,” explains Franco. “And at the end of the day, these same issues have worsened under Trump’s administration, under Republican control. So people, I think, are looking for someone who’s going to explain what’s happening and propose solutions and be dogged about finding them.”

title: Nicaragua’s Future: Repression, Resistance, and Hope
content:
Register


Over the past two decades, Nicaragua has experienced one of the world's most dramatic declines in freedom, losing 49 points on Freedom in the World’s 100-point scale assessing political rights and civil liberties. The regime of Daniel Ortega and his wife and “co-president” Rosario Murillo has systematically dismantled democratic institutions, imprisoned political opponents, killed peaceful protestors, and shuttered thousands of civil society organizations, independent media outlets, and religious institutions. Moreover, it has exported its repression beyond Nicaragua's borders, targeting dissidents in neighboring Costa Rica with surveillance, intimidation, and violence. The regime has also deepened its cooperation with other authoritarian powers, including those ruling China, Cuba, Russia, and Iran.

title: Egypt’s crackdown on independent media reaches Mada Masr as editor faces trial
content:
Egypt convicted Mada Masr’s Lina Attalah in a hearing marred by violations, and ordered it closed

Originally published on Global Voices

Lina Attalah. Photo from Mada Masr website, used with permission.

A crackdown on independent media in Egypt is escalating.

The latest wave of suppression of the country’s last remaining critical voices began with the violent arrest of the entire newsroom of Matsada2sh, a fact-checking and open-source intelligence (OSINT) page that relies on social media and is run by young journalists. 

The six-person team was forcibly disappeared, illegally detained, and interrogated under torture for several days before being charged with terrorism and spreading false news. They remain in pretrial detention.

The crackdown then reached Mada Masr, one of Egypt’s most prominent independent outlets, and its founder and editor-in-chief, Lina Attalah. On November 11, Attalah is due to stand trial for the second time in two weeks, this time on charges of spreading false news that carry a possible prison sentence.

title: Japan: Raise Rights With Vietnam’s Leader
content:
(Tokyo) – Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi should urge Vietnamese President To Lam to make concrete progress on human rights during his official visit to Japan from November 8 to 11, 2026, Human Rights Watch said today.

Human Rights Watch wrote to Prime Minister Takaichi expressing concerns about Vietnam’s intensifying crackdown on human rights. The repression violates obligations that Vietnam accepted under the 2018 Comprehensive and Progressive Agreement for Trans-Pacific Partnership, to which Vietnam and Japan are parties.

“The Vietnamese government has broken its pledges for reform and continues to crack down on basic freedoms,” said Kanae Doi, Japan director at Human Rights Watch. “Prime Minister Takaichi should communicate clearly and publicly to President To Lam Japan’s serious concerns about human rights and labor rights violations.”

The Vietnamese government has sharply intensified its repression of basic freedoms over the past decade, Human Rights Watch said. To Lam served as Vietnam’s minister of public security from 2016 to 2024, heading the country’s national police force. He is now both general secretary of the Communist Party of Vietnam and president.

title: Op-ed | The Children We Cannot Afford to Overlook
content:
Conflict and humanitarian crises have devastating consequences for healthcare systems, often leaving children without access to essential medical treatment. Yet the need for surgical care does not disappear when international attention shifts elsewhere. In this piece, Yusra Mardini and Sarah Masiyiwa explore why children’s surgical care must be a priority in humanitarian responses and long-term recovery.

In December 2024, the fall of the Assad regime, after nearly 14 years of devastating civil war, brought hope to many Syrians. But the end of a regime does not mean the end of a country’s suffering. When Yusra returned to Syria in 2025, ten years after being forced to leave her home, she found a country both familiar and profoundly changed. Beyond the physical destruction lay the enormous challenge of rebuilding the services and institutions people depend on every day.

Among them is surgical care for children.

title: Ilmastopolitiikka 1,5 asteen riskirajan ylityksen jälkeen
content:
Niko Humalisto on luontopolitiikan dosentti Itä-Suomen yliopistosta ja Suomen Lähetysseuran ilmastoasiantuntija. Hän vaikuttaa ilmastoneuvotteluissa kansainvälisen kehitys- ja humanitaaristen järjestöjen Act Allianssin teknisenä asiantuntijana. Vapaa-ajalla hänet löytää Turun polkupyöräpajalta.

Tulevassa Turkin COP31-ilmastokokouksessa ei voi enää uskottavasti vaatia ripeitä toimia  lupaamalla, että 1,5 asteen kuumenemisen rajan ylitys voidaan välttää. Tämän tieteellisiin riskirajoihin perustuvan velvoittavan tavoitteen epäonnistuminen ei kuitenkaan käynnistä ennalta määrättyä erityismenettelyä. Osapuolet joutuvat kehittämään uusia keinoja ylläpitää ilmastotoimien kunnianhimoa ja reagoimaan tulevaisuuteen, jossa sopeutumistoimien ja ilmastotuhojen painoarvo kasvavat.   

YK:n ympäristöohjelma UNEP kertoi syyskuussa, että maapallon keskilämpötilan nousua yli 1,5 asteen ei enää käytännössä voida välttää. Raportin optimistimmassakin skenaariossa lämpeneminen käy noin 1,8 asteessa. Tällainen polku edellyttäisi voimakkaita ja pitkäjänteisiä päästövähennyksiä tilanteessa, jossa monenkeskinen yhteistyö sakkaa ja kansainvälinen ilmastorahoitus ei ole lähelläkään riittävää tasoa.

title: Why I'm still paying the price of being a mother
content: It’s 9.30. After feeding two sleepy humans aged three and six, getting them ready and walking them to school, I’ve finally sat down at my desk to do some work – paid work I should say – and write this piece I’ve been putting off since the beginning of September. I've been thinking about it ever since I read the report on the motherhood penalty that the Haut Conseil à l’Égalité (HCE), a French national advisory body, published right in the middle of the back-to-school rush, a particularly stressful time of year for a working mother. Until the afternoon school's clubs started less than a month ago, I had to leave my desk every day at 15.30 to pick up the children, while my partner was still at the office. The rest of the day, I'd take them to the park, run their baths, and make dinner. So, yes, motherhood has meant less time to work – and less income. Around a third less than before having children. Sadly, I’m no exception. The same is true of mothers in France, where I come from, in the years following the birth of their first child. title: Mercator Switzerland Foundation joins IJ4EU as co-funder
content:
Mercator Switzerland Foundation has joined the Investigative Journalism for Europe (IJ4EU) programme as a new co-funder, helping sustain public-interest reporting across the continent and beyond.

The Swiss foundation joins the Dutch Adessium Foundation, the Norwegian Fritt Ord Foundation, and the German Free State of Saxony in providing co-funding alongside core financing from the European Union’s Creative Europe programme.

Mercator backs pioneering projects, invests in civil society organisations, and builds broad alliances to advance its vision of a democratic, equitable, and ecologically sustainable society. Its work includes strengthening journalism and ensuring people have the information they need to participate in democratic life.

Its financial contribution to the 2026-27 edition of IJ4EU will help fund activities delivered by the programme’s implementing partners: the International Press Institute (IPI) in Vienna, the European Journalism Centre (EJC) in Maastricht, and the European Centre for Press and Media Freedom (ECPMF) in Leipzig.

title: Nepal Anti-Graft Body Charges Ex-PM Madhav Nepal, 96 Others With Corruption
content:
Nepal’s anti-corruption agency on Tuesday filed corruption charges against former Prime Minister Madhav Kumar Nepal and 96 others over an alleged land-swap scheme that investigators say cost the government roughly $4.8 million.

The case, brought by the Commission for the Investigation of Abuse of Authority (CIAA), centers on the illegal sale of land that should have been returned to government ownership, according to a commission statement.

The CIAA also charged Minendra Prasad Rijal who served as minister for federal affairs and parliamentary affairs and coordinator of the cabinet’s social committee at the time of the alleged scheme.

“Summons will be issued for all of them starting tomorrow to appear in court,” Parwati Hitan, the Special Court’s information officer, told OCCRP. She said defendants will have 15 days to appear, and that this can be extended by seven days. None has been detained.

“Once they appear, their statements will be recorded, and after their statements, the hearing process moves forward,” Hitan said. Witness statements and evidence would follow before a bench issues a final decision, she added.

title: How We’re Covering the Midterms — and the Aftermath
content:
This has been a midterm election cycle unlike any other. Wealthy donors spent staggering sums. Both parties moved to redraw congressional district lines. President Donald Trump and his allies relentlessly questioned whether the results could be trusted even before a single ballot was counted. At Trump’s direction, the Justice Department filed a lawsuit that said the federal government would contest any outcome in which Sen. Dan Sullivan, the Republican incumbent in Alaska, was not victorious.

Newsrooms, including ours, have tried to plan how we will cover an election in which the losing side refuses to accept the will of the voters. Was the Alaska lawsuit a single data point or a harbinger?

As we prepare to write about Nov. 3 and beyond, we find ourselves in the uncomfortable position of trying to game out what might happen in the future — not our strong suit. The record shows that journalists are pretty good at telling readers what happened, particularly if we have some time and some data to sift through, and much less good at forecasting the future.

title: Joulun tilitys lähestyy – tee ääniteilmoitus ja tarkista omat tietosi
content:
Joulun tilitys maksetaan viikolla 50. Huolehdithan ääniteilmoitukset kaikista jo julkaistuista biiseistä meille viimeistään 16.11., jotta ne ehtivät mukaan joulun tilitykseen.

Tarkista myös omat tietosi, kuten tilinumerosi ja veroprosenttisi MyGramex-portaalista ennen tilitystä. Puutteelliset tiedot voivat estää korvausten maksun ja joudut odottamaan rahojen maksua seuraavaan tilitykseen asti.

Joulun tilityksessä maksetaan korvauksia mm. radiosoitosta (ajalta heinä-syyskuu 2026), taustamusiikista sekä ulkomailta. Sekä lisäksi korvauksia on demand-, netti-PVR- ja kopiointikäytöstä.

Korvaussummat tulevat näkyviin MyGramexiin lähempänä maksupäivää. Korvauserittelyt näkyvät MyGramexissa maksupäivän jälkeen.

  • Tee muutosverokortti ensin OmaVerossa.
  • Odota hetki, jotta Verohallinto päivittää uuden verokortin tietoihinsa.
  • Tämän jälkeen palaa MyGramexiin ja hae uusi verokorttisi klikkaamalla “Hae Verokortti Verohallinnosta” -painiketta. Muutos päivittyy näkyviin portaalissa hetken kuluttua.

title: Suomen Arkkitehtiliiton asiantuntijalausunto: RTS 26:26-28 Asunnon tilat, asuinhuoneet ja oleskelutilat sekä keittiöt ja ruokailutila
content:
Suomen Arkkitehtiliitto kittää mahdolisuudesta lausua asuntosuunnittelua käsittelevistä ohjekorttiehdotuksista asunnon tilat, asuinhuoneet ja oleskelutilat sekä keittiöt ja ruokailutilat. Ohjekorttiehdotuksissa esitetty mitoitus edustaa hyvää asuntosuunnittelua, ja on hyvä, että ne ohjaavat esimerkilliseen mitoitukseen. Tilavarausten huomioiminen esimerkiksi lämpöpattereiden vaatiman tilan osalta on sisällytetty kattavasti ohjekortteihin. Käytännön asuntotuotannossa tilojen mitoitusta on trendinomaisesti kiristetty aikaisempien korttien hyvistä ohjeista huolimatta, ja toivomme näilä ohjekorteilla olevan ohjausvaikutusta asuntosuunnitteluun tulevaisuudessa. Alla esitämme kehitysehdotuksia ohjekortteihin:

Ohjekorttien havainnollisuutta lisäisi porrashuoneen esittäminen esimerkiksi vinjettikuvana, jolloin asunnon suhde koko rakennukseen kävisi ilmi periaatetasolla. Mikäli “Asuntosuunnittelu. Asunnon tilat” -kortin tavoitteena on toimia muut kortit kokoavana ohjeena, ehdotamme että sen roolia suhteessa muihin asuntosuunnittelun ohjekorttisarjan kortteihin selvennetään ja täydennetään tältä osin.

title: Search launched for new CEO of CMI – Martti Ahtisaari Peace Foundation
content:
CMI – Martti Ahtisaari Peace Foundation today launches a search to find its next CEO. The application period is open until 17 November.

The new Chief Executive Officer will lead the organisation and help shape the future of peacemaking.

Founded by Nobel Peace Laureate Martti Ahtisaari, CMI is an independent peace mediation organisation that works to prevent and resolve political conflicts through dialogue and mediation.

CMI brings people together who might not otherwise meet, builds trust across political divides and supports those closest to a conflict in shaping their own paths towards peace.

The organisation hopes to find an internationally experienced senior leader who combines a strong understanding of diplomacy and peace processes with executive leadership experience.

The position is based in Helsinki, Finland. The recruitment process is carried out in cooperation with MPS. Read the full role description here and apply by 17 November 2026.

title: Mobilisation without realignment
content:
Israel’s October 2026 elections produced a striking paradox. After three years of devastating wars, the failures surrounding 7 October, growing international isolation and deep domestic divisions, Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s governing bloc has lost its parliamentary majority. Yet Likud remains the largest party, and Netanyahu’s electoral performance was considerably stronger than many had anticipated.

According to the final count published by the Central Elections Committee on 29 October, Netanyahu’s bloc won 53 seats, compared with 48 for the Jewish-led opposition and a historic 19 for Arab parties; official certification is due on 4 November. This leaves 67 seats outside Netanyahu’s bloc, opening several possibilities for political change. However, the result should not be interpreted as an ideological shift towards the left. Much of the opposition consists of security-oriented centrists, nationalists and right-leaning liberals who explicitly distance themselves from Social Democracy.

content:
Kansanmusiikista syntyy valitettavan harvoin koko kansan ilmiöitä. 90-­luvulla Värttinän Miinan laulu kyllä sai aikaan mediakohun, ja 2000-luvulla Loituman Ievan polkka virisi viraalihitiksi. Nyt meillä on jälleen kappale, jonka kaikki tietävät: Antti Paalasen Takatukka.

Uuden musiikin kilpailun yllättäjä saa seurakseen muita vetäviä kappaleita Paalasen pitkäsoitolla Haitarimarinadi. Valloittavia, elämänmyönteisiä, kujeilevia ralleja, joista kuntosalille sopii Aerobikki ja illanistujaisiin Ihan vaan käymään.

Tilanteen niin vaatiessa pohjalaiset pelimannisävelmät soivat kurtussa kurinalaisesti juuri niin kuin perinne velvoittaa, mutta soolotuotannossaan tämä hurja hanuristi ja komia kurkkulaulaja on luonut jotain sellaista, mitä meillä ei muuten olisi. title: In Praise Of Japan’s Failure To Keep Up
content:
TOKYO — Nothing triggers the bog-walloping Fenian in me quite like a visit to the British Embassy. This one, with its fine Georgian-revival facade, looked on my last visit a decade ago like a lost Cotswold manor-house brought to life in Tokyo.

But what was it that I found so unsettling? Perhaps the stately setting? Or its gilt-framed displays of a preternaturally regal, late queen? Her gaze following me about the room as I moved among the fine art and mahogany, like those creepy Sacred Heart of Jesus portraits I grew up with. Me, a lad reared in an Irish republican home where the Queen’s annual Christmas messages were as welcome as a poltergeist.

To the more clubbable, the embassy’s English country house manner would have seemed merely civilized; a demonstration that Merrie England had acquired over generations the ability to arrange the upholstery without the aid of an AI shepherd.

title: ‘National priority’ policies claim to solve Europe’s housing crisis. They may make it worse
content:
Housing shortages and soaring rents are central to Spain’s upcoming general election. As each party presents voters with ways of addressing the crisis, far right party Vox is backing a simple solution: the principle of prioridad nacional, or “national priority”, which would put Spaniards first in line to receive government benefits.

The policy is central to Vox’s programme. It proposes expanding social housing with priority for Spanish nationals, alongside deregulation and tax reductions.

It is presented as a common sense solution, but national priority does not actually address the root causes of scarcity. In fact, it could even make them worse.

The housing crisis, like many crises, has winners as well as losers: while tenants struggle, landlords collect higher rents and enjoy rising asset values. National priority does not change or tackle these underlying inequalities. Instead, it merely ranks neighbours by entitlement to assistance, while also sowing the seeds of social division.
