title: How North Korea became a world leader in state-sponsored hacking
content:
Binance, the world’s largest cryptocurrency exchange, was the victim of a massive heist in late October. Approximately US$6.36 billion (£4.74 billion) of funds were stolen within the space of 20 minutes in an attack that has been described as the largest of its kind in history.

The source of the attack has not yet been officially confirmed. But the FBI and blockchain analytics company TRM Labs identified North Korea’s TraderTraitor hacking unit as the group most likely to have been behind it. Two other blockchain analytics firms, Chainalysis and Elliptic, have supported this attribution.

This is not the first time North Korea has been linked to cyber-attacks. Several other cryptocurrency exchange thefts in recent years have been attributed to North Korean state-sponsored hackers. These include the 2019 Upbit and 2025 Bybit hacks, where funds worth US$42 million and US$1.5 billion respectively were stolen.

Therefore, while Pyongyang has always denied any involvement in state-sponsored cyber warfare, it is not surprising that North Korea has once again been mentioned in connection with a major crypto heist.

title: Baltic Sea Region mental health work presented at the WHO Regional Committee for Europe
content:
The approach of the Baltic Sea Region Mental Health Platform was presented to health ministers and delegates of the 53 Member States of the WHO European Region at the 76th session of the WHO Regional Committee for Europe (RC76), held in Copenhagen on 27-29 October 2026. Ülla-Karin Nurm, Director of the NDPHS Secretariat, which leads the platform and coordinates Policy Area Health in the EU Strategy for the Baltic Sea Region, took the floor under three agenda items.

A session with mental health on the agenda

The Regional Committee is WHO’s decision-making body in the European Region and sets the direction for regional health policy. This year, Member States adopted “Ageing is living”, the regional strategy on healthy ageing for 2026-2030. They were also consulted on a new strategy to tackle noncommunicable diseases (NCDs) and advance well-being through health promotion, due for adoption in 2027. WHO/Europe also raised the possibility of a complementary regional strategy on mental health and well-being for the same period, which is still under discussion. The consultation comes 40 years after the Ottawa Charter for Health Promotion.

title: Suomen tukema rahasto auttaa tunnistamaan Ukrainan sodan vainajia
content:
Ukrainassa toimiva uusi DNA-laboratorio on auttanut tunnistamaan lähes 200 sodassa kadonnutta henkilöä kolmen ensimmäisen toimintakuukautensa aikana. Laboratorion perustamista on tuettu Partnership Fund for a Resilient Ukraine (PFRU) -rahastosta, jota Suomi rahoittaa yhteensä 8,8 miljoonalla eurolla vuosina 2022–2027 osana Suomen kahdenvälistä kehitysyhteistyötä Ukrainassa. Suomen lisäksi rahastoa rahoittavat Viro, Ruotsi, Norja, Sveitsi, Iso-Britannia ja Kanada.

Ukrainassa on tällä hetkellä yli 100 000 sotaan liittyvää kadonnutta henkilöä, ja yli 18 000 vainajaa odottaa tunnistamista. Kadonneet henkilöt ovat valtaosin rintamalla kadonneita sotilaita.  Rikosteknisten laboratorioiden määrä on yli kaksinkertaistunut hyökkäyssodan alkamisen jälkeen.

PFRU on tukenut DNA-laboratorion perustamista yhden Ukrainassa toimivan alueellisen rikosteknisen laboratorion yhteyteen. Uusi alueellinen DNA-laboratorio on mahdollistanut vainajilta otettujen näytteiden tutkimisen paikallisesti ja auttanut purkamaan tunnistustutkimusten ruuhkaa kasvavan tarpeen keskellä. Laboratorion kolmen ensimmäisen toimintakuukauden aikana on pystytty tunnistamaan lähes 200 kadonnutta henkilöä.

title: Trifectan jatko vai sininen aalto? Katsaus Yhdysvaltain välivaaleihin 2026
content:
Välivaaleissa ratkaistaan senaatin ja edustajainhuoneen enemmistö. Vaikka demokraatit voittaisivat, kovin suuria muutoksia Yhdysvaltain politiikkaan tuskin on tulossa.

Marraskuun alussa pidettävät Yhdysvaltojen välivaalit ovat herättäneet keskustelua laajalti myös Suomessa. Välivaaleihin lähdetään tilanteesta, jossa republikaanipuolueella on Donald Trumpin presidenttiyden lisäksi enemmistö sekä senaatissa että edustajainhuoneessa.

Tämä republikaanien niin sanottu Trifecta on koossa pienimmän mahdollisimman enemmistön turvin: 218 edustajaa sekä yksi itsenäinen edustaja, joka äänestää republikaanien mukana, kun taas demokraattipuolueen edustajia on 214. 

Välivaalien seurauksena ratkaistaan edustajainhuoneen 435 paikan enemmistö sekä senaatin enemmistö, kun senaattoreista kolmasosa on uudelleen ehdolla.

Presidentti Trumpin historiallisen alhainen kannatus, yhdysvaltalaisia äänestäjiä huolestuttava talouden tila sekä esimerkiksi Iranin sota povaavat menestystä vaaleissa demokraateille.  Republikaanit voivat silti pärjätä vaaleissa kohtuullisesti vaalijärjestelmän, johtuen vaalijärjestelmän erityispiirteistä sekä vaaleihin ja vaalijärjestelmään kohdistuneista toimenpiteistä.

title: Gazan tulitauko on olemassa vain paperilla, sanoo yli sata järjestöä
content:
Lokakuussa 2025 alkaneesta tulitauosta on kulunut vuosi, mutta Gazan tilanne on kohentunut vain vähän. Näin arvioi yli 100 järjestöä yhteisessä kannanotossa. Mukana ovat muun muassa Pelastakaa Lapset, Norjan pakolaisneuvosto ja Amnesty International.

Järjestöjen mukaan Israelin iskut ja sotilasoperaatiot ovat tappaneet tulitauon aikana yli 1 400 palestiinalaista, joista yli 300 on lapsia. Gazan terveysministeriön tuoreimman luvun mukaan kuolleita on ainakin 1 480 ja loukkaantuneita yli 5 200. Israel on perustellut iskujaan Hamasin muodostamalla uhalla.

”Tulitauko on merkityksetön, jos lapsia tapetaan edelleen eivätkä perheet vieläkään pysty rakentamaan elämäänsä uudelleen”, sanoo Pelastakaa Lasten pääsihteeri Inger Ashing tiedotteessa.

Norjan pakolaisneuvoston pääsihteeri Jan Egeland kutsuu tilannetta häpeälliseksi.

”On äärimmäisen häpeällistä, että kokonainen vuosi tulitauon voimaantulon jälkeen palestiinalaisten tilanne Gazassa on kohentunut niin vähän”, Egeland sanoo.

title: UK climate minister Katie White: COP31 must respond to ‘really scary’ science
content:
The upcoming COP31 climate talks in Antalya, Turkey need to respond to the latest science on global warming, which is “really scary”, says UK climate minister Katie White.

In an interview with Carbon Brief setting out the UK’s priorities for the summit, White also responds to suggestions that the government is walking back its climate policies.

White says the “shocking” impact of extreme heat and wildfires this summer makes it clear that climate change “isn’t something far off; it’s something we’re living through”.

She adds that the UK will be working to “hold up the science”, including the Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change (IPCC) reports that should be the “basis of discussions”.

The COP31 presidency push on electrification is “going to be key”, says White, who points to other priorities for the UK that include tackling methane emissions and reducing deforestation.

White says the recent approval of the Jackdaw gas field in the North Sea is “fully in line” with carbon budgets and that the UK continues to support the “transition away from fossil fuels”.

title: Asevelvollisuusarmeija ja etenkin reserviupseerikoulutus ovat suomalaisen onnellisuuden kova ydin
content:
Puolustusbudjettiamme olisi syytä pohtia laajempien yhteiskunnallisten vaikutusten kautta. UKK-instituutin johtaja sanoo, että paras koskaan tehty keksintö kansanterveyden kohentamiseksi on yleinen asevelvollisuus. Jos vaikuttaa asevelvollisuus kansanterveyteen, niin takuuvarmasti se on myös tehokas kotouttaja. Aikuisuuden kynnyksellä vietetty aika asevelvollisena vaikuttaa yksilöön ja sitä kautta yhteiskuntaamme monin tavoin, joita eivät kriitikot ehkä ole tulleet ajatelleeksi.

Julkaisin RUK:n ”Jaarli” (nr. 183) -kurssimme 40-vuotisjuhlan kunniaksi kirjan, jossa pohdin asevelvollisuuden ja etenkin reserviupseerikoulutuksen merkitystä suomalaiselle yhteiskunnalle. Alun perin idea lähti vain siitä, että tiesin monien kurssitoverieni pärjänneen hyvin elämässä ja ajattelin heidän minibiografioidensa kiinnostavan muitakin kuin kurssikavereita. Olihan joukossa sentään niin Janne Jaakkola, Risto Siilasmaa kuin edesmennyt rocktähti Pete Wallikin. Monista muista kiinnostavista, jos ei niin tunnetuista nimistä puhumattakaan. Henkilökuvia tuli lopulta 19 ja siihen päälle omat RUK-muistelut.

title: What a Storm Overflow Alert Leaves Unsaid – Spilling The Truth Workshops (14 and 24 September 2026)
content:
by Jakleen Al-Dalal’a

When an overflow map reports that a discharge has stopped, what does that tell someone standing beside the water?

The map may no longer show an active release. It cannot necessarily tell them what was discharged, how much entered the river, where it has travelled, or whether other sources of pollution are present. Yet people may consult that same map before swimming, taking children paddling, or bringing a group of volunteers to the river.

title: Hyvinvoinnin historiaa -teos tietokirjallisuuden Finlandia-ehdokkaaksi – "Teos on erityisen ajankohtainen nyt"
content:
Antti Kariston ja Jussi Simpuran teos Hyvinvoinnin historiaa: Ajankuvia Suomesta (Gaudeamus) on valittu vuoden 2026 tietokirjallisuuden Finlandia-ehdokkaaksi. Jo kolmanteen painokseen edennyt tutkijoiden teos esittelee tuokiokuvia hyvinvoinnista itsenäisessä Suomessa ja osoittaa, että laajasta käytöstään huolimatta hyvinvointi ei ole yksiselitteinen käsite. Se on myös muuttunut ajassa paljon.

Sosiaaliturva ja sähkövalo, oppivelvollisuus ja olympiahenki, kirjastot ja kahvinjuonti… Mistä kaikesta puhumme, kun puhumme hyvinvoinnista? Antti Kariston ja Jussi Simpuran Hyvinvoinnin historiaa on aikamatka suomalaiseen yhteiskuntaan ja elämään itsenäisyyden vuosikymmeninä.

Helmikuussa ilmestynyt teos kuvaa, miten hyvin Suomessa on milloinkin voitu ja mitä on pidetty hyvänä elämänä – sekä miten hyvinvointia on haviteltu ja mistä sitä on luultu löytyvän. Itsenäisyyden ensiaskeleista kuljetaan läpi sotavuosien, hyvinvointivaltion rakennuksen, kasinotalouden ja lamavuosien.

title: Soviet Animations of Winnie the Pooh, Created by the Innovative Animator Fyodor Khitruk
content:
In 1962, the animator Fyodor Khitruk made his directorial debut with Story of One Crime, a film that broke with a Soviet tendency to make imitations of Disney-style animations. The film, as The Guardian explained in its 2012 obituary for the animator, came as a shock. It was stylistically simple and dealt with themes that Disney films would never touch — like, why would a polite clerk murder two housewives with a frying pan?

Khitruk made other films that were packed with social commentary, often taking aim at abuses in the Soviet system. But, he also made straightforward animations for children, none more famous than his series of films based on AA Milne’s beloved Winnie the Pooh books.

Created between 1969 and 1972, Khitruk’s three films star a bear named “Vinni-Pukh” who looks nothing like the Winnie the Pooh that Westerners grew up with. (You can see the original illustrations of Pooh by E.H. Shepard here.) But viewers will certainly recognize the storyline and spirit of the original Pooh in the Soviet adaptations. For decades, these films have enchanted East European viewers, both young and old. And they still occasionally appear on Russian TV.

title: A Tungsten Truce – Allies Cannot Compete for Access
content:
Maine-headquartered Elmet Group bought 4.99% of Vietnam’s Masan High-Tech Materials for about $125m on October 1. Alongside the stake, Masan agreed to supply and process about 1,250 metric tons of tungsten trioxide equivalent annually for at least eight years.

Alarm bells rang in Brussels, where internal European Union documents warned competition from partner countries could disrupt Europe’s access to Vietnamese critical minerals, Reuters reported. Masan is a key tungsten supplier to the continent, particularly Germany, and the immediate question is who will be served first if supplies run short.

The annual volume committed to Elmet equates to about 1,000 metric tons of tungsten metal. That is roughly a third of Vietnam’s estimated 2025 mine output. It also represents about 4.4% of broader European tungsten end-use demand in 2025, which Fastmarkets estimates at 28,700 metric tons of tungsten trioxide equivalent.1

Tungsten, about two and a half times as dense as iron, is used in missile components and armor-piercing ammunition.

title: Privacy's Defenders Podcast: The Secret Room
content:
The government’s surveillance powers grew rapidly after Sept. 11, 2001, some in public view and some in secret. EFF suspected but couldn’t prove that the National Security Agency was spying on Americans' communications. The New York Times sat on a story about it for over a year, finally publishing it in December 2005. Then, in January 2006, a retired AT&T technician named Mark Klein walked into EFF's office with a manila folder of documents that blew the story wide open. 

Welcome to the third episode of “Privacy’s Defenders,” a podcast about the people – lawyers, journalists, hackers, and others – who’ve fought to secure your digital liberties since before most people even knew what the internet was.

(You can also find this episode on the Internet Archive and on YouTube.)

Responding to the news that the French War Crimes Unit has opened a judicial investigation into a deadly November 2024 Israeli strike on a civilian building in central Beirut, following a legal complaint filed by French-Lebanese artist and filmmaker Ali Cherri and the International Federation for Human Rights, Amnesty International’s Regional Director Heba Morayef said: 

The opening of this judicial investigation by the French War Crimes Unit is a critical, long-overdue step towards making a dent in the wall of pervasive impunity enjoyed by Israeli forces for war crimes committed in Lebanon.  

Heba Morayef, Amnesty International

title: Democratic Socialists on the Rise: Darializa Avila Chevalier & Claire Valdez Set to Win House Seats
content:
New York City is preparing to send two DSA members, presumptive election night winners Darializa Avila Chevalier and Claire Valdez, to Capitol Hill. DSA-backed candidates made historic gains in this year’s Democratic primaries, with at least five expected to join current DSA members Rashida Tlaib and Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez in the House. But can socialism really make headway in the halls of Congress? Democracy Now! fellows Amba Guerguerian and Diego Ramos report.

“Our task is going to be winning our colleagues over to our position and finding common ground,” Valdez tells Democracy Now! “Some of the most popular policies in our country’s history have been socialist policies,” says Avila Chevalier. “They have been the things that working people have organized for and won.”

title: After the Election: Revitalizing Serbian Democracy, and Lessons from the Opposition Victory
content:
Sun shining through a Serbian flag. (Photo Credit: Ivan Radic on Flickr CC BY 2.0)

Last month Serbia’s Student List, a youth-backed opposition movement, won parliamentary elections, ending 14 years of rule by longtime Serbian leader Aleksandar Vučić and his Serbian Progressive Party (SNS). The broad coalition grew from an ongoing protest movement sparked by the collapse of a renovated canopy at Novi Sad’s train station in 2024, which killed more than a dozen people and was widely blamed on government corruption.

Political rights and civil liberties had eroded significantly under Vučić’s rule as the government placed legal and extralegal pressure on the political opposition, independent media, and civil society organizations. As a result, Serbia’s Freedom in the World status declined from Free to Partly Free in 2019. Its score has since continued to decline, now registering 53 points on Freedom in the World’s 100-point scale—the lowest score in the western Balkan region and the second-lowest score in all of Europe. Turnout in the election was reported at a massive 70 percent, reflecting Serbian citizens’ desire for reforms in their country.

title: Changes to Chile’s Human Rights Institute Risk Leaving Victims Behind
content:
Chilean President José Antonio Kast introduced in Congress on October 19 a proposal to change the country’s National Human Rights Institute.

Founded in 2009 as an autonomous state body, the institute has worked to promote and protect human rights in Chile, including by taking legal action on behalf of human rights abuse victims.

If passed, the legislation would weaken some of the tools the institute uses to protect human rights and diminish its independence.

The bill would remove the institute’s eleven-member board of directors, replacing them with a new five-member transitional board that would draft new bylaws for the institute. Unlike the current board, which has four members who were selected directly by civil society groups, the new transitional board would be proposed by the president, approved by the Senate, and would have no members selected directly by civil society. This sits uneasily with the standards set out in the Principles relating to the Status of National Human Rights Institutions (the Paris Principles), which recommend that members be independent from the government and selected through a process that ensures broad civil society representation.

title: UK ministers told not to engage formally with Indian mega-zoo after lobbying
content:
Guardian and Mongabay reveal approaches to officials and MPs on behalf of Vantara zoo ahead of UK-chaired Cites meeting on endangered animal imports

British government ministers were told not to engage formally with Vantara, the controversial mega-zoo run by the Indian billionaire Anant Ambani, after lobbying efforts by the private animal sanctuary in the run-up to a UK-chaired meeting on the trade in endangered species, according to documents.

This week, the UK heads a 32-country committee meeting in Geneva of Cites, the United Nations body that regulates trade in endangered species. The meeting will examine how India has responded to compliance concerns about imports of endangered animals.

title: I took a five-star ride to the front line
content: At the beginning of Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine, it was still relatively easy to get to Kramatorsk, a city in eastern Ukraine's Donetsk region. I remember my first trip in 2022, by train. I travelled from Kyiv to Kramatorsk on an old Soviet-era train, packed with soldiers and smelling of onions, cold cigarettes, and sweat. Since then, I have used almost every possible way of getting there. By car, bus, Sprinter van, and car rental. But the closer Russian forces moved towards the city, the harder it became to reach. Trains to Kramatorsk stopped running in 2025. Then car-rental companies pulled out of the area, and we could no longer hire cars. “We have trackers on them,” one rental company employee once told me in Kyiv, giving me a threatening look. “Don’t try to fool me.” I took the bus that day. By the end of 2025, getting to Izium, 120 kilometres south of Kharkiv, was still relatively easy. The problem was getting from there to Kramatorsk, another 70 kilometres south. As Russian drones increasingly targeted the road, the vans stopped running. We only discovered this once we were already in Izium, in late October. title: World of Warcraft: Forever Is Already Overrun with AI Slop
content:
World of Warcraft: Forever, a re-imaginging of the legendary MMO, comes out Wednesday. The idea is to recapture the feeling of discovery and wonder players had when adventuring across its world for the first time back in 2004.

But 2026 is a very different time. Subreddits dedicated to the game are already overrun with AI-generated addons that rip off longtime developers’ work, and a company that helps players track their damage output tells me it is making changes to its API because of the inundation of AI slop addons.

title: DRC Orders Probe into Illegal Mining Following Major Copper and Cobalt Seizure
content:
The Democratic Republic of the Congo will open an investigation into suspected mining fraud and widespread illegal mining, following the seizure of thousands of tons of copper and cobalt as well as more than 500 trucks and other machines, according to a statement by the Justice Ministry.

The probe comes two weeks after Congo's mines minister suspended the head of the state agency overseeing artisanal and ​small-scale mining, accusing him of failing to prevent illegal ‌mining on licensed concessions.

As the world’s largest producer of cobalt and second-largest producer of copper, the Democratic Republic of the Congo has long struggled with unauthorized miners and cross-border smuggling rings encroaching on industrial concessions held by foreign operators.

title: I Was There to Document the Aftermath of Deadly Flooding. Then, It Started Raining.
content:
Three summers ago, over Father’s Day weekend, my family and I went camping in the Lincoln National Forest, just a few hours drive north of our home in El Paso, Texas. It’s a beautiful area that’s long served as a getaway for the region, with skiing in the winter, and golf and hiking in the summer. My daughter played under the trees, and I rode my bike down mountain trails that, I noticed, seemed concerningly dry. 

The next evening, after we left to drive home, two fires started in forests surrounding the town of Ruidoso, New Mexico, around 25 miles away from where we’d been. I watched horrifying videos online of fire lapping the mountains behind the village’s strip malls and parking lots. The fires were eventually suppressed by a combination of human effort and the late summer monsoon season. But when the downpour of rain hit the burnt landscape around Ruidoso, it created another problem: Recurring floods then ripped through town, damaging homes and infrastructure, and leading to emergency rescues.

title: From Wales to Finland, minority language speakers still face prejudice
content:
“How very rude to be speaking Welsh.”

That was the complaint a stranger directed at Patsy, a Welsh learner featured in my latest book, after overhearing her family speaking Welsh in a Cardiff cafe. She could hardly believe it: “But you’re in Wales. What are you talking about?”

Wales has come a long way since the days of the Welsh not, a wooden token often accompanied by corporal punishment that was used in some 19th-century schools to discourage children from speaking Welsh. The Welsh language is now more visible, more widely supported and more politically protected than at any point in history.

But my ongoing research of Welsh-speaking families living in Cardiff suggests that while attitudes have improved dramatically, some linguistic prejudice still lingers beneath the surface. The pattern is not unique to Wales. I found similar experiences among Finland’s Swedish-speaking minority, where official recognition of the language has not always translated into acceptance in everyday life.

title: Greenpeace: Energian hinnannousu selitti koko euroalueen inflaation kiihtymisen
content:
Riippuvuus fossiilisista polttoaineista käy kalliiksi Greenpeacen analyysin mukaan. Energian hinnat olivat syynä euroalueen inflaation koko nousulle 1,7 prosentista 3,2 prosenttiin tämän vuoden tammikuun ja elokuun välisenä aikana, järjestö tiedottaa.

Ilman Iranin vastaisen sodan aiheuttamaa öljyn hintashokkia euroalueen inflaatio olisi ollut elokuussa Greenpeacen mukaan vain 2,2 prosenttia 3,2 prosentin sijaan. Riippuvuus fossiilisista polttoaineista jättää kotitaloudet alttiiksi hintojen arvaamattomille nousuille, millä on laajempia vaikutuksia koko talouteen.

”Ongelma on suurempi kuin mikään yksittäinen konflikti tai öljyn hintapiikki. Niin kauan kuin taloudet pysyvät sitoutuneina heittelehtiviin fossiilisten polttoaineiden markkinoihin, toistuvat häiriöt nostavat kotitalouksien kustannuksia", Greenpeace Internationalin energia-asiantuntija John Noël sanoo järjestön tiedotteessa.

title: State of the climate: 2026 likely to tie with 2024 as the warmest year on record
content:
• A record August and the second-warmest year to date
  • A record-setting El Niño event
  • Record heat across much of the world
  • Good odds of being world’s warmest year 
  • Datasets are split on whether 2026 is headed for a record
  • 2027 very likely to be the warmest year on record
  • Earth’s energy imbalance has more than doubled
  • Arctic sea ice minimum tied for 10th lowest, Antarctic near record lows

    • With three-quarters of the year now past, it is virtually certain that 2026 will be the warmest or second-warmest year on record.

    A rapidly strengthening El Niño, alongside human-caused global warming, made this year’s August the warmest on record and September the second-warmest. 

    El Niño is the warm phase of a recurring climate pattern in the tropical Pacific that releases heat from the ocean into the atmosphere and temporarily boosts global temperatures.

    Carbon Brief’s analysis gives 2026 a 67% chance of surpassing 2024 as the warmest year on record across an average of six global temperature datasets. 

    In January, it is likely the groups that report global surface temperatures will be divided on whether 2026 officially beat 2024’s record.

title: Kutsu: Kirjanjulkistus Tampereella 9.11. – Jaana Vuoren uusi tiedeteos avaa empiiristä tutkimusta ihmistieteissä
content:
Tervetuloa! Jaana Vuoren uuden teoksen Johdatus empiiriseen tutkimukseen ihmistieteissä julkistustilaisuus järjestetään Tampereella kulttuuriravintola Telakan yläkerrassa maanantaina 9.11.2026 kello 16.30 alkaen. Jaana Vuoren kanssa keskustelee sosiologian yliopistonlehtori Mikko J. Virtanen.

Sukupuolentutkimuksen professori emerita Jaana Vuoren uusi teos Johdatus empiiriseen tutkimukseen ihmistieteissä on kirjoitettu ensimmäiseksi korkeakoulutasoiseksi tutkimusmenetelmiä käsitteleväksi oppikirjaksi ihmistieteissä. Niitä ovat humanistiset ja yhteiskuntatieteet sekä monet tieteidenväliset alat.

title: Mali: Still no accountability six months after abduction of pro-democracy politician Mountaga Tall and his son
content:
Malian authorities must urgently disclose the fate and whereabouts of lawyer and pro-democracy politician Mountaga Tall and his son Cheick Mamadou Tall, Amnesty International said six months after their abductions.

On the night of 3 May 2026, just days after a series of attacks by armed groups across Mali, Mountaga Tall, leader of the National Congress for the Democratic Initiative (Congrès national pour l’initiative démocratique), was abducted from his home in the capital, Bamako, by armed and hooded men driving vehicles without registration plates.

Cheick Mamadou Tall, his eldest son, went missing on 16 May after allegedly receiving a telephone call from his father asking him to bring personal effects. He left his home to deliver the effects and never returned. His fate has remained unknown since then.

title: Ethiopian Authorities Suspend Independent Newspaper
content:
In what has become the new normal, the Ethiopian government has silenced yet another independent media outlet.

The Ethiopian Media Authority announced in a November 2 Facebook post that it is indefinitely suspending the print and online license of the Reporter, one of Ethiopia’s oldest media institutions. Publishing in English and Amharic, the Reporter is also the country’s last privately owned Amharic newspaper.

Stating that the suspension would take effect immediately, the Media Authority accused the Reporter of violating the country’s laws and media ethics by repeatedly publishing content that was against “national interests.” The authority added that the outlet published “distorted content that negatively affects foreign investment, tourism, and diplomacy.”

The action is part of the government’s ongoing assault on the media and civic space in the country and points toward increasing use of vague claims about “national interests” to shut down any critical reporting.

title: I’m a journalist in Türkiye, but I’m not in jail (yet)
content: In May, I bumped into my colleague Tuğba Tekerek at a gathering of Turkish journalists in Istanbul. “Freelancers should come together and look out for one another,” she said. “Sure,” I told her. “Let's brainstorm soon.” We never got the chance. Tuğba and I both worked at Deutsche Welle Turkish, although at different times. In 2024, she traveled to Georgia to report for a range of outlets, including LGBTI+ rights association Kaos GL. She's now in jail because of that reporting. When I started out as a journalist in 2010, losing a job didn't necessarily mean the end of a career. A colleague who was laid off could usually find another position. Today, stories like Tuğba's are becoming all too common. Türkiye is due to hold its next scheduled elections in 2028, unless an early vote is called. As we approach that date, media outlets critical of the governement are increasingly coming under pressure, and being taken over by state-appointed trustees, one by one. title: Vibe Coded AO3 Clone Site Down After Fanfic Authors Buried It With 2,000 Takedown Notices in a Single Day
content:
A vibe-coded site that scraped Archive of Our Own (AO3) fanfiction works, reuploaded them and charged for audiobook versions is down now after the creator said they received over 2,000 takedown requests from authors in the single day it was up.

ao3.life, a website that sprung up following last week’s announced weeks-long outage of fanfiction repository AO3, scraped the internet for works to populate the site using “a swarm of AI Agents controlling 40 virtual machines were scraping the internet for all drives, scrapes, and sources,” the site’s creator, named Ganesh, wrote on a page apologizing for the entire project. AO3.life went down on Monday evening following widespread backlash from readers and authors on social media. 

Before it went down, the ao3.life homepage said, “AO3, saved before it slips away. Search every fandom, ship and trope. Read it here, keep the EPUB, or let it read to you when your eyes get tired.”

title: Serbian Bank Tied to Outgoing Regime Collapses After Internal Vault Theft
content:
A Serbian commercial court officially launched bankruptcy proceedings against Belgrade-based Alta Banka on Tuesday and activated a state mechanism to refund depositors, just one day after top executives were arrested for allegedly stealing more than 45.5 billion Serbian dinars (more than $427 million) from the institution's vault.

The financial collapse stems from a massive alleged internal theft. In coordinated statements on Monday, the Public Prosecutor's Office for Organized Crime and the Interior Ministry confirmed the detention of the "responsible person" of Alta Banka, identified by authorities only by the initials D.M. (born 1981). The Serbian branch of regional N1 TV subsequently identified the suspect as Davor Macura. Also arrested were the director of the treasury and cash management department, G.M. (born 1987), and a treasury associate, I.P. (born 1982).

Macura is suspected of abusing his position to illegally extract the funds, defrauding Alta Banka of exactly 45,556,596,250 dinars—an amount worth more than $427 million—according to the Interior Ministry and the Public Prosecutor’s Office for Organized Crime.

title: Canada-EU alliance: as a blueprint for a ‘middle-power bloc’ it has a lot of hurdles to overcome
content:
The dream of a Canada-EU “middle-power bloc” has hit its first serious obstacle. At the Montreal summit, Brussels failed to deliver on the promise of associate membership for Canada, despite the enthusiastic backing of European Commission president, Ursula von der Leyen.

Instead, the EU offered the hollow consolation of “an ever-closer association”, raising an uncomfortable question about whether the middle powers can overcome their own divisions to become a serious geopolitical force.

The two-day EU-Canada summit culminated on October 30 with the launch of a so-called “Alliance for the Future”. That compromise formula of association, rather than associate membership – which specifically ruled out full membership – was necessary because of internal disagreements in the EU.

In September, Von der Leyen, offered Canada the chance to become the EU’s first “associate member”. But Germany, backed by Greece and others, objected to the term, worried about legal uncertainty and the expectations it might raise in other countries.

title: Väitös: Podcast-yhteisöjen voima rakentuu osallistumisesta, vuorovaikutuksesta ja oppimisesta
content:
Podcastien ympärille muodostuvat yhteisöt voivat lisätä jäsentensä yhteenkuuluvuuden tunnetta, osallisuutta ja hyvinvointia. KM Juska Wendlandin väitöstutkimus osoittaa, että osallistumisen ja vuorovaikutuksen lisäksi myös oppimiskokemukset vahvistavat yhteisöjä. Tutkimus tarjoaa media-alalle käytännön työkaluja podcast-yhteisöjen rakentamiseen ja arvioimiseen.

Juska Wendlandin mediakasvatuksen alan väitöstutkimus on kansainvälisesti uraauurtava avaus podcast-yhteisöjen tutkimukseen. Se tarkastelee, mitkä tekijät rakentavat yhteisöllisyyden kokemusta podcastien ympärille ja miten kuulijat sitoutuvat yhteisöihin.

Wendlandin mukaan monet menestyneet podcastit ovat rakentaneet asemansa nimenomaan vahvan yleisösuhteen avulla. Silti aidosti yleisölähtöinen sisällöntuotanto on yhä harvinaista.

title: World Court Set to Rule in Myanmar Genocide Case
content:
(The Hague) – The International Court of Justice has announced that it will deliver its judgment on November 19, 2026, in the case brought by Gambia against Myanmar for alleged violations of the Genocide Convention, Human Rights Watch said today in releasing a question-and-answer document on key issues in the case.

In August 2017, Myanmar’s security forces began a sweeping campaign of massacres, rape, and arson against ethnic Rohingya in northern Rakhine State that forced more than 700,000 people to flee to neighboring Bangladesh. In November 2019, Gambia filed a case before the International Court of Justice alleging that Myanmar’s atrocities against the Rohingya constitute genocide and violate the Convention on the Prevention and Punishment of the Crime of Genocide. This is not a criminal case against individuals, but a request for a legal determination of Myanmar’s state responsibility for genocide.

title: Seven Arrested in International Operation Targeting Investment Fraud
content:
Authorities from seven countries seized more than 100 servers and arrested seven suspects of  investment fraud that may have costed victims in at least 50 countries more than $4.6 million. 

Tuesday’s operation, led by German prosecutors and supported by Europol and Eurojust, targeted a company that operated in Cyprus and Israel and supplied platforms to criminal groups running call centers in Albania, Kosovo and North Macedonia. 

The scheme relied on misleading online advertisements promising high returns from cryptocurrency, foreign exchange and stock trading. Victims were encouraged to make larger deposits after their accounts showed fictitious profits, but then withdrawals were subsequently blocked. The investigation began in 2022 after a German couple reported being unable to recover their investments.

title: Naisjohtaja vei perheyrityksen lähes kuuden miljoonan liikevaihtoon ilman sijoittajakonkareita hallituksessa
content:
Suomalainen, naisvetoinen ja ilman sijoittajia kasvanut Saaren Taika perustaa ihonhoitonsa kahdeksaan riippumattomaan kliiniseen tutkimukseen

Perniö, 3.11.2026. Naisten perustamat yritykset saavat vain murto-osan pääomasijoituksista. Perniöläinen kosmetiikkayritys Saaren Taika on silti kasvanut ilman niitä lähes kuuden miljoonan euron liikevaihtoon. Toimitusjohtaja Veera Amnelin-Kylämäki on johtanut äitinsä Johanna Amnelinin perustamaa yritystä jo kuusi vuotta. Tämän vuoden tavoite on ylittää kuusi miljoonaa euroa, ja Saaren Taian tuntee nimeltä jo 56 % suomalaisista.

Kliiniset tutkimukset rahoitetaan yleensä sijoittajien rahoilla, mutta Saaren Taika on maksanut kaikki kahdeksan riippumatonta kliinistä tutkimustaan itse. Ne on tehty seitsemällä valmiilla tuotteella ihotautilääkärin valvonnassa. Tutkimukset kattavat iho-ongelmat, joiden kanssa moni kamppailee eniten: ruusufinniin taipuvan ihon punoituksen, akneen taipuvan ihon, psoriasikseen taipuvan päänahan, kuivuuden ja kutinan, ikääntymisen merkit sekä tummat silmänaluset.

PwC:n selvityksen mukaan naisyrittäjät tarvitsevat kasvuun ennen kaikkea lisää verkostoja ja rahoitusosaamista (PwC 2024).

title: Türkiye: European Court to Rule on Istanbul Mayor’s Detention
content:
The Turkish authorities are misusing powers of detention and prosecution against opposition politicians in Türkiye to prevent them from participating effectively in elections or political life, the Turkey Litigation Support Project, Human Rights Watch, and the International Commission of Jurists said today.

The three groups have submitted a third-party intervention—or amicus brief—to the European Court of Human Rights with information on patterns of human rights violations, abuse of the criminal law, and the erosion of judicial independence in Türkiye. The intervention was made in a case brought by the Istanbul mayor and opposition politician Ekrem İmamoğlu to the Strasbourg court asserting that his detention violates his rights protected under provisions of the European Convention on Human Rights, including article 5 (right to liberty and security), article 18 (limitation on use of restrictions on rights), and article 3 of Protocol No. 1 to the convention (right to free elections).

title: Stone-age hunters in northern Europe may have used poison arrows to hunt big prey
content:
Autumn walks in Britain are glorious, as the foliage changes colour and cool crisp air begins to bite. However, some of these European trees hide a much darker secret. For example, the lovely red cup-shaped structures on a yew tree, known as arils, conceal seeds that carry dangerous toxins. These toxins may have been used to poison arrow tips in the past.

A new Danish study has shown that the “smoking gun” is not the poison itself, but the size of the small arrowheads used to deliver the toxin into the hunted animal.

The authors of the latest research examined Danish stone tool technology from the period immediately preceding the arrival of farming in Europe – the Mesolithic.

They argue that the distinctive small size of stone arrow tips from the early Mesolithic period (about 9,000–3,950BC) suggest they were used to hunt large prey with the help of poisons. The poison has long since vanished, leaving only the stone tip.

Arrows that do not use poison are typically larger, since they need to damage the animal’s flesh. But poisoned arrows need only wound a prey animal enough to allow the poison to enter the blood stream.

title: A Better Future for Science? Reflections from Beijing
content:
Dr. Pragya Chaube is Assistant Professor at the UPES University, India. She is a co-chair of the CODATA Connect Early Career Network and co-founder Open Science South Asia Network (OSSAN). Pragya’s participation in the International Science Council’s (ISC) Midterm Membership Meeting and Beijing Science Dialogue was kindly supported by the ISC and by the China Association for Science and Technology (CAST).

I had the opportunity to spend the week of 19–24 October in Beijing, alongside a large gathering of scientists and representatives of national science academies from across the globe, reflecting on the future of science. More than 1,000 people from over 80 countries and regions came together for these discussions. We welcomed a new ISC President, Robbert Dijkgraaf, and, on the final day, adopted the Beijing Science Declaration: Science in a Complex World, Science for a Better Future.

The meeting covered many important issues, but I left Beijing reflecting on a question that connects many of them for me: What kind of research ecosystem do we want to build for the future, and what needs to change to get there?

title: Small structures. Big impact!
content:
Scientific advances have enabled technologies that manipulate the total wavefunction of molecular systems through controlled confinement, thereby altering their physical, chemical, optical, and electronic properties. Despite these breakthroughs, our understanding of how to precisely control matter at the quantum level remains in its early stages. The confinement of molecular systems is a pervasive phenomenon across chemistry, physics, biology, astrochemistry, and engineering.

The COSY COST Action, Confined molecular systems: from a new generation of materials to the stars aimed to advance the understanding and control of confined molecular systems and to translate the resulting knowledge into practical applications.

These efforts range from developing new materials, including biomaterials with strong potential for industrial use, to understanding the chemistry behind molecular processes in space. To achieve these goals, COSY combined advanced experimental techniques for synthesising and characterising new nanomaterials with state-of-the-art theoretical modelling.

title: Firm Productivity and the Composition of Jobs in the Green Economy: Factor Reallocation with Heterogeneous Clean Destinations
content: We study the macroeconomic consequences of emissions reductions in a model with heterogeneous firms, search-and-matching frictions, endogenous technology adoption, and sector-specific capital adjustment costs. Extending the framework of Finkelstein Shapiro and Metcalf (2023) and calibrating to Finland, we distinguish between high- and low-productivity clean technologies within a three-sector framework. Our results show that an emission reduction policy implemented via a carbon tax induces modest losses in output and consumption, as part of the reallocation away from emissions-intensive sector is absorbed by lower-productivity clean sector. By contrast, the standard two-sector model with a single clean technology shows slightly positive output effects due to a greater increase in average firm productivity. These findings highlight that the macroeconomic costs of climate policies depend on the productivity composition of the expanding clean sector. Within the emissions-intensive sector, emissions are mainly reduced through abatement activities, but the degree of factor reallocation is still substantial: under the baseline calibration, employment in the emissions-intensive sector declines by nearly one-quarter in response to a 40% emissions reduction target. Lower abatement costs reduce the extent of factor reallocation required to achieve a given emissions reduction target.

content:
Marraskuun alussa vietetään kansainvälistä RSV-tietoisuusviikkoa. Suomessa RSV-kausi käynnistyy yleensä marras–joulukuussa, ja tartuntoja on eniten vuodenvaihteen molemmin puolin. Virukselle on tyypillistä syklinen esiintyminen, jolloin voimakkaampi RSV-epidemia toistuu noin joka toinen vuosi.

Suomessa laboratoriovarmistettuja RSV-tapauksia todetaan vuosittain noin 4000–8000, epidemiakauden voimakkuudesta riippuen. Todellinen tartuntojen määrä on kuitenkin virallisia tilastoja suurempi, sillä valtaosa lieväoireisista hengitystieinfektioista sairastetaan kotona ilman laboratoriotestejä.

RSV voi aiheuttaa ikääntyneille vaikean taudin ja olla pahimmillaan hengenvaarallinen

RSV on merkittävä vakavan infektion aiheuttaja pienten lasten lisäksi myös ikääntyneillä. Ikäihmisillä RSV voi johtaa sairaalahoitoon ja siihen voi liittyä huomattava kuolleisuusriski. Riski sairastua vaikeaan tautimuotoon kasvaa iän myötä, etenkin jos henkilöllä on perussairauksia.

title: Fem projekt fick stöd från de ungas kultur- och språkprogram Volt
content:
De samlade projektansökningarna representerar såväl uttrycksformer som film, litteratur och fotografi som ljudkonst och poesi. Projekten har närmat sig tillhörighet på många sätt.

– De projekt som fått höga poäng har haft väldigt konkreta ansökningar och en taktil approach till hur man går till väga för att förstå tillhörighet, säger Randi Samsonsen, den beslutsfattande sakkunniggruppens ordförande.

– Ett gemensamt kriterium för de som stöds är också att de barn och unga som projektet berör verkligen möts i det verkliga livet, att saker ska ha möjlighet att uppstå genom verkliga möten. Bland de stödda projekten är detta ett kvalitetsperspektiv, och inte bara ett kvantitetsperspektiv, förklarar Samsonsen. 

Nordic Lunch Stories är ett ungdomsdrivet grönt konstprojekt som för samman 12–15-åringar från Finland, Sverige och Danmark. Genom ljud, berättande, scenkonst och matkultur skapar ungdomarna tillsammans ett konstnärsresidens, ett flerspråkigt ljudlandskap och en offentlig presentation om hur vi kan leva hållbart i vardagen.

title: Suden matkassa -näyttely huipentuu taiteilijatapaamiseen
content:
Lokakuun ajan Ikimetsägalleriassa esillä ollut Suden matkassa -näyttely huipentuu lauantaina 7.11. taiteilijatapaamiseen, jossa taide, metsät ja musiikki kohtaavat.

Näyttelyn teokset tarkastelevat sutta luonnon monimuotoisuuden, rinnakkaiselon ja ihmisen luontosuhteen näkökulmista. Mukana ovat kuvataiteilijat Samuli Heimonen ja Minna Pyykkö sekä valokuvataiteilija Juha Suonpää, joiden lähestymistavat samaan aiheeseen ovat keskenään hyvin erilaisia.

Päivän ohjelma käynnistyy klo 12.30 Juha Suonpään esityksellä Kun metsä vielä katsoo. Videoista koostuva esitys rakentuu seitsemän vuoden aikana metsään sijoitettujen kameroiden tallentamista hetkistä sekä tekstistä, äänestä ja hiljaisuudesta. Teos tarkastelee metsän läsnäoloa, muistia ja katoamista sekä elämää, joka jatkuu omassa rytmissään ihmisen katseen ulottumattomissa.

Esityksen jälkeen Suonpää, Pyykkö ja Heimonen kertovat taiteestaan, työskentelystään ja näyttelyn taustoista. Tilaisuus tarjoaa harvinaisen mahdollisuuden keskustella taiteilijoiden kanssa heidän teoksistaan ja susiaiheen herättämistä ajatuksista.

title: A Beginner’s Guide to Philosophy: From Logic to Epistemology to Metaphysics
content:
These are, perhaps, not the very best times for humanities majors. Seldom do we even hear the once-standard defense that, by pursuing a course of study in subjects of that kind, students “learn how to think.” Such a justification still points to real value, at least in the most demanding settings. Take Harvard’s course Humanities 10, whose digital device-free environment and syllabus covering everything from The Odyssey and Ulysses to Plato and James Baldwin — at a pace of one substantial book per week — recently drew the attention of the Wall Street Journal. Yet it’s always been true that you don’t have to major in anything to learn how to think, or in any case, to make a start of doing so.

Take the philosophy-and-literature YouTuber Jared Henderson, who in the video at the top of the post tells us how he began his self-directed study in high school. “I did what a lot of people would think is natural,” he says. “I went to a bookstore, and then I just found some books that I wanted to read.” The pieces of light reading he took home: Friedrich Nietzsche’s The Birth of Tragedy and Martin Heidegger’s Introduction to Metaphysics.

title: How China Might Target US Midterms
content:
No research shows Chinese propaganda or disinformation playing a pivotal role in the midterm elections, particularly when compared to Russia’s aggressive attempts. Yet significant blind spots exist. If it desired, Beijing is well-positioned to shape political debate through the WeChat app and through Chinese AI models.

Rather than shifting control of Congress, Beijing’s goal would likely be to reduce the presence of known Communist Party critics, particularly those serving in the Congressional-Executive Commission on China. Created by Congress in October 2000, the Commission monitors Chinese human rights and rule of law.

Several competitive races feature Commission members, including former Senator Sherrod Brown in Ohio and current Commission Chair Dan Sullivan in Alaska. House races in Iowa and Virginia involve current Commission members Zach Nunn and Jen Kiggans. Ashley Hinson, who is running for the Senate in Iowa, is on the House Select Committee on the Chinese Communist Party, another Congressional body critical of the regime.

title: Digitalpolitik, gibts das auch für die Gesellschaft?
content:
Digitalpolitik ist Gesellschaftspolitik. Wer unsere digitalen Räume und Werkzeuge gestaltet, gestaltet auch die Art, wie wir zusammenleben. Die OKF wie die breitere digitalpolitische Zivilgesellschaft bringt dieses Argument seit Jahren vor und setzt sich für Wege der demokratischen, gerechten und grundrechtskonformen Technikgestaltung ein. Mit KI, dem Bau von Rechenzentren und der Nachfrage nach Chips hat sich das Thema nun auch auf die physische Infrastruktur unserer Gesellschaft ausgeweitet.

In der Digitalpolitik dominieren heute aber andere Narrative. Auch das noch junge Bundesministerium für Digitales und Staatsmodernisierung verengt den Diskurs. Es darf bei Digitalpolitik aber nicht bloß um Souveränität, Wettbewerbsfähigkeit und Sicherheit gehen. Geht es um digitalpolitische Programme, wollen wir uns nicht mit dem Eurostack und Deutschland-Stack zufrieden geben. Wir fordern den Gesellschafts-Stack.

title: EU Commission to probe supermarket cyberattacks
content:
BRUSSELS — The European Commission will assess how well supermarkets are prepared to handle cyberattacks after refrigerators in dozens of stores across at least six EU countries were taken offline.

EU Agriculture and Food Commissioner Christophe Hansen told POLITICO that the attacks would be discussed at the next meeting of its Security College to assess retailers’ contingency plans and their ability to respond to incidents.

“Europe’s food supply chain must be prepared for new and evolving threats,” Hansen said. “The repeated cyberattacks on supermarkets are deeply concerning, causing economic losses for retailers and empty shelves for consumers.”

The announcement follows dozens of supermarkets across Europe reporting disruptions to their refrigeration and freezing systems on Monday.

Incidents were reported in at least six EU countries — Belgium, Luxembourg, Sweden, Ireland, the Netherlands and Estonia — with some retailers reporting that refrigerator temperatures had suddenly surged to as high as 50 degrees Celsius.

title: A year after the military coup: authoritarian practices dash Gen Z aspirations for a new Madagascar
content:
By Nciko wa Nciko

A year since Colonel Michael Randrianirina seized power in a military coup, Madagascar finds itself far from the refoundation that he promised. Instead, his first year in power has been marked by the military’s consolidation of power and the expansion of authoritarian practices. News outlets abound with commentaries assessing Randrianirina’s first year in power. The grievances and demands that led thousands of Gen Z protesters to the streets, including chronic water and electricity shortages and endemic corruption, remain unresolved.

Just like his predecessor Andry Rajoelina, Randrianirina has quickly turned to the law to unduly consolidate power, suppress dissent, instrumentalize anti-corruption efforts against political opponents, and shield his administration from efforts to bring accountability for killing and maiming protesters and for corruption. He has also weaponized the law to restrict civic space by characterizing freedom of association as criminal conspiracy and attempted to secure online mass surveillance powers over dissenting voices to make it difficult for them to critique his regime’s (mis)management of public affairs.

title: "Princes and Thieves" Author Matthew Cole on Jared Kushner & the "Secret Plot to Remake Middle East"
content:
Vanity Fair recently published an excerpt from longtime investigative reporter Matthew Cole’s new book, Princes and Thieves: Jared Kushner and Mohamed bin Zayed’s Secret Plot to Remake the Middle East.

The excerpt alleged that during President Trump’s first term, Saudi and Emirati leaders secretly put at least $2 billion into bank accounts and gave access to Kushner. At the time, Jared Kushner was serving as senior adviser to President Trump, his father-in-law. He is now Trump’s special envoy. Kushner’s lawyers responded by demanding that Vanity Fair retract the article and threatening legal action against the book publisher, Simon & Schuster.

Jared Kushner denied the report, saying, “The allegations made by this author are completely insane, categorically false, and never happened. We denied every one of these claims on the record, yet the author failed to provide a single shred of evidence to substantiate any of them.” His lawyers say no such bank accounts existed and that the allegations are unsupported by the verifiable evidence.

title: Zambia: Widespread Repression in Post-Election Crackdown
content:
(Johannesburg) – The Zambian police and military forcibly disappeared, arbitrarily detained, beat, and threatened opposition members and supporters as well as lawyers, journalists, and government critics in the days before and after general elections in August 2026, Human Rights Watch said today. The authorities have also yet to credibly explain or investigate the killing of an opposition leader in contested circumstances.

“Zambia’s government should break this dangerous cycle of repression,” said Ashwanee Budoo-Scholtz, deputy Africa director at Human Rights Watch. “The authorities should immediately halt the ongoing post-election crackdown, allow access to lawyers and provide medical care for those in detention, release everyone arbitrarily detained, and ensure accountability for abuses by security forces.”

title: Gaza’s Ceasefire Leaves Palestinians Trapped Behind a Moving Line
content:
UN rights officials warn that repeated displacement, attacks near encampments and restrictions on shelter materials are making return increasingly difficult.

By Ramesh Jaura

BERLIN | 2 November 2026 (IDN) — A ceasefire may have reduced the scale of fighting in Gaza, but it has not ended the displacement of Palestinians. Nor has it given most families a realistic prospect of returning home.

The United Nations Human Rights Office, OHCHR, warned on 30 October that Israeli military operations continued to force Palestinians into ever-smaller areas of the Gaza Strip. Homes and public infrastructure were still being destroyed, displacement sites had come under attack, and families were being pushed away from areas close to the Israeli-controlled “Yellow Line”.

“The nightmare of displacement in Gaza is both acute and chronic,” said Ajith Sunghay, head of the UN Human Rights Office in the Occupied Palestinian Territory.

Many Palestinians displaced before the ceasefire cannot return because their former neighbourhoods lie beyond the Yellow Line. Others have been uprooted repeatedly from places where they sought temporary shelter.

title: The Killers of Journalists Are Getting Away with Murder. Governments Must Act to End Impunity.
content:
On the International Day to End Impunity for Crimes Against Journalists, IFEX exposes the gulf between governments’ commitments to media freedom and their failure to deliver justice. From the unprecedented number of journalists killed in Gaza to the question of who ordered the assassination of Daphne Caruana Galizia in Malta, those responsible continue to evade accountability. Meanwhile, civil society organisations and international institutions pursuing accountability face growing pressure.

The murder of a journalist is rarely an isolated crime. It is an attempt to suppress information, obstruct scrutiny and deny the public the truth. When perpetrators escape justice, sources are silenced, colleagues are intimidated and those who abuse power emboldened.

More than 100 IFEX member organisations document attacks, support journalists at risk and demand accountability. The scale of the crisis is stark: nine in ten cases involving the killings of journalists and media workers go unpunished.[1] In 2025, the Committee to Protect Journalists (CPJ) recorded 129 journalists and media workers killed, the highest annual toll since the organisation’s records began in 1992.[2]

title: Suomi katsoo Keski-Aasiaan
content:
Viime vuosina Suomen kaupalliset, kulttuuriset ja poliittiset suhteet Keski-Aasiaan ovat tiivistyneet ja suomalaisyritysten vienti on moninkertaistunut erityisesti Uzbekistaniin ja Kazakstaniin. Keskiaasialaisten muuttoliike Suomeen on myös kasvanut nopeasti. Alue tarjoaa yksilöille ja yrityksille uusia seikkailuja ja mahdollisuuksia, mutta suhteiden kehitykseen liittyy monia kysymysmerkkejä.

Venäjän keisarikunta ja britti-imperiumi kilpailivat jo 1800-luvulla ns. ”Suuressa pelissä” Keski-Aasian hallinnasta. Brittiläinen maantieteilijä Sir Halford Mackinder määritteli vuonna 1904 esittämässään sydänmaateoriassa Keski-Aasian ja sitä ympäröivät Euraasian alueet maailman geopoliittiseksi ”kääntöpisteeksi”, jonka päätyminen yhden mannermaisen valtakunnan haltuun johtaisi pahimmassa tapauksessa länsimaisen vaikutuksen katoamiseen koko Euraasian mantereelta. Mackinder kannatti siksi ensimmäisen maailmansodan jälkeisessä Euroopassa Venäjän patoamista reunavaltioiden ketjulla. Entinen Venäjän keisarikunnan ja Neuvostoliiton eteläraja on säilynyt siitä asti tärkeänä geopoliittisena jakolinjana, jonka toisella puolella avautuu nyt varsin dynaaminen ja monikasvoinen maailma.

title: In the name of the father, the son, and AI
content: The hyperrealistic image on the wall of the Church of Saint Mary Magdalene in Novolukoml, Belarus, shows a young man in jeans, holding a laptop in one hand and a rosary in the other. It depicts Carlo Acutis, nicknamed the “cyber-apostle” and often described as the first millennial saint. Fittingly, AI helped create it. The image was created by three people: a photographer, a designer, and an AI engineer. It was blessed on 11 October by Archbishop Tadeusz Kondrusiewicz, the former head of the Catholic Church in Belarus. The parish described it as the first such image in the country. But who was Carlo Acutis? Born in London to Italian parents, the teenager became known for promoting Catholicism online, earning him the nickname “God's influencer”. He died of leukaemia in 2006, aged just 15. In 2025, Pope Leo XIV canonised him, making him a saint. Despite all the work involved behind the image, the use of AI as sparked criticism online. title: Inside the Secretive, Contradictory World of Campaign Ads Funded by AI Super PACs
content:
Sign up here to receive Bellingcat’s biggest investigations by email as soon as they are published. Become a member and support our work here.

An online ad for Ben McAdams, the Democratic candidate for Congress in Utah, emphasised that he could be trusted because he “fought back against MAGA”.

In Texas, another ad promoted Republican candidate Chris Gober, calling him a “MAGA warrior”.

What’s interesting is that both ads were ultimately paid for with money from the same organisation – Leading the Future (LTF), a Super PAC which opposes regulations that “constrain” innovation in AI. The network has received US$125 million in funding in total from OpenAI president Greg Brockman, his wife Anna Brockman, tech-focused venture capital firm Andreessen Horowitz (a16z) and a16z’s founders, Federal Election Commission (FEC) filings show. 

Directly opposing LTF is Public First Action (PFA), which calls for AI safety regulations and guardrails. PFA has received $40 million in funding from AI company Anthropic. 

Like the ads run by organisations funded by LTF, the Super PACs funded by PFA also ran ads that appeared supportive or critical of Trump depending on the voters they were targeting.

title: There is now an alternative to Russian gas – but not yet to soaring prices
content:
According to GIE AGSI, the public gas storage platform for European gas infrastructure, Slovakia is currently receiving 486 GWh of gas per day, while withdrawals are approaching 615 GWh daily. With the heating season under way, an increasing share of these withdrawals is going directly to household consumption.

The energy content of the gas currently in storage stands at 20.5 TWh, representing 54.28% of Slovakia’s maximum gas storage capacity. This is below both Hungary’s storage level (77.5%) and the EU average (75%). Only Latvia has a lower figure in the statistics, at 50%.

At the same time, Slovakia’s storage capacity relative to its consumption is considerably higher than the EU average. Of the 3.5 billion cubic metres that can be stored, the majority – approximately 2.75 billion cubic metres – is held in NAFTA’s storage facilities near Láb, close to the Austrian and Hungarian borders.

These facilities are ideally positioned to receive and store both Russian gas arriving via TurkStream through Serbia and Hungary – at least for the time being – and gas delivered from Austria, including LNG unloaded at terminals in northern Germany.

content:
A new NORDIS report reviews 14 media literacy events and campaigns across the Nordic countries, highlighting lessons learned and a growing focus on artificial intelligence. The partners now aim to build on these experiences by equipping teachers and librarians with tools to help young people navigate an increasingly AI-driven information landscape.

The new NORDIS report Literacy events and campaigns documents what the NORDIS partners Faktabaari, Faktisk.no (Tenk), TjekDet and Källkritikbyrån delivered between May 2024 and October 2026.

They are in short:

  • 3 events and 11 campaigns in Finnish, Norwegian, Danish, Swedish and English.
  • AI and recommendation algorithms as the common challenge to digital infomation literacy, from the Faktabaari AI Guide for Teachers (launched at the NORDIS Digital Information Literacy Forum in Helsinki, January 2025) to Tenk’s AI teaching package and search course in Norway and TjekDet’s “Hey Chat… Who Should I Vote For?”material ahead of the Danish election in March 2026.

title: Indonesia Asks Russia to Stop Recruiting Its Citizens for Ukraine War
content:
Indonesia’s government has asked Russia to cease recruiting its citizens to fight in the war against Ukraine after new data showed a surge of Indonesians joining the conflict.

The growth in mercenary recruits comes amid Indonesian government concerns that citizens of the Southeast Asian country have been tricked into joining the Russian military under the guise of civilian employment.

"The Indonesian government has asked the Russian government to take the necessary steps to ensure that Indonesian citizens are not recruited into the military or other military-related formations in Russia through any means," Indonesian Foreign Ministry spokeswoman Yvonne Mewengkang said in a statement reported Sunday by state news agency Antara.

Mewengkang said Indonesia requested to be added to a list of countries whose citizens are exempt from official Russian military recruitment, Antara reported, adding she expected the measure to be implemented “effectively and as soon as possible.”

title: After ProPublica Investigation, House Democrats Demand Answers on U.S. Citizens Detained by Immigration Agents
content:
What Happened: Citing ProPublica’s recent investigation, House Democrats are again asking the Trump administration to explain why hundreds of U.S. citizens have been held by immigration agents and how the government verifies citizenship during immigration operations.

In an October letter to Department of Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin, California Rep. Lou Correa and 39 other legislators demanded the administration share the number of citizens that immigration agents have detained and how the government is tracking such encounters. They also asked for more information about how agents are trained to verify citizenship and legal status.

Why It Matters: ProPublica counted more than 500 Americans detained by immigration agents — almost certainly an undercount since the government is not transparently tracking the cases.

title: Traces of dinosaur blood found in world-first discovery
content:
A 115-million-year-old fossil dinosaur bone encased in a dense mat of microbes found in Brazil contains tiny structures resembling red blood cells, and molecular traces of blood.

Along with colleagues from Brazil, Japan and the United States, we’re reporting the discovery today in the Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences.

This is the first direct molecular evidence of compounds from dinosaur blood preserved within structures that look like red blood cells. The find offers an unprecedented window into the biology of extinct animals.

It also expands what we thought possible: that fossils can preserve soft tissues and biomolecules such as blood over millions of years.

We studied a fossil specimen of a small dinosaur called Aratasaurus museunacionali, found in the Romualdo Formation in northeast Brazil.

The Romualdo Formation is renowned for its exquisitely preserved fish, turtles, crocodile relatives and pterosaurs. It also contains rare dinosaur material. The site’s unique geochemical conditions have preserved fossils with fine anatomical detail rarely seen elsewhere.

title: Koronapandemia paljasti heikkouksia pohjoismaisessa yhteistyössä
content:
Koronapandemian päätöksenteossa painotettiin kaikissa Pohjoismaissa aiempien yhteistyösopimusten sijasta EU-politiikkaan perustuvaa yhteistyötä.

Pohjoismainen yhteistyö kylmän sodan ajasta aina 2020-luvulle on keskittynyt hyvinvointivaltioidean pohjalle, ja maat ovat pyrkineet vahvistamaan ja vaalimaan yhteistyötään eri aloilla. COVID-19-pandemian puhjettua pohjoismainen yhteistyö jäi kuitenkin konkreettisemman Euroopan unionin yhteistyön jalkoihin.  

Kansainvälisen politiikan apulaisprofessori Laust Schouenborg esittää vuonna 2012 julkaistussa kirjassaan The Scandinavian International Society arvion, jonka mukaan koko pohjoismaisen yhteisön perustana on hyvinvointivaltioidea. Vaikka yhteiseurooppalainen integraatio on EU:n myötä levinnyt erityisesti työvoima- ja kulttuurialoille, hyvinvointivaltioideaan perustuva pohjoismainen yhteisö on pitänyt pintansa EU:n rinnalla.

Pohjoismaisen yhteisön erityispiirteisiin kuuluu esimerkiksi kansalaisten tasa-arvo, laaja liikkuvuus sekä edullinen terveydenhuolto. Näitä piirteitä on pyritty vahvistamaan vielä 2000-luvullakin erilaisilla yhteistyösopimuksilla.

title: Saimaannorppa valtaa takaisin vanhoja vesiään, kanta elpyy hitaasti
content:
Saimaannorpan kanta jatkaa varovaista kasvuaan, tiedottaa Metsähallitus. Leudot talvet ja kalanpyydyskuolemat hidastavat kannan elpymistä.

Uusimman kanta-arvion mukaan Saimaalla elää tällä hetkellä 545 yksilöä, ja kasvua viime vuodesta on 15 saimaannorpan verran.

Viime talvi oli poikkeuksellisen vähäluminen ja kevät tuli aikaisin. Tänä vuonna havaituista kuuteista lähes 90 prosenttia syntyikin apukinoksiin ja keinopesiin. Pesäpoikaskuolleisuus on sekin ollut viime vuosina suurta, joskin tarkka arviointi on asiantuntijoiden mukaan haastavaa.

“Talvien lauhtumisen myötä perinteiseen lumipesälaskentaan perustuvan kanta-arvion epävarmuus kasvaa. Siksi kanta-arviossa hyödynnetään nykyään aiempaa monipuolisemmin myös muita havaintoaineistoja. Jo aloitettua menetelmäkehitystä jatketaan uudessa LIFE-hankkeessa", kertoo Metsähallituksen Luontopalveluiden erityisasiantuntija Miina Auttila tiedotteessa.

Tulevaisuudessa tavoitteena on parantaa laskennan tarkkuutta matemaattisella mallilla, jossa voidaan hyödyntää laajasti erilaisia seuranta-aineistoja.

title: Museums Don’t Need More Visitors. They Need More Contributors.
content:
Above: Anna Stolyarova with the mural Tolerance

On a wall in Amsterdam’s Nieuw-West district, a mural called Tolerance is fading away. Nobody is rushing to restore it. And yet it is still part of a museum collection.

That collection belongs to Street Art Museum Amsterdam (SAMA), a museum without a building. Its hallways are the neighbourhood’s streets. Its artworks are the walls. Its visitors are the people who live there, who are also its contributors and, as founder Anna Stolyarova likes to point out, its sharpest critics.

A museum whose collection is quite literally vanishing has had to face questions most institutions can put off. Who creates cultural value? Who decides what is worth passing on? And what is a museum for when the knowledge it needs already exists outside its walls? SAMA’s approach to citizen science in museums offers a challenge to the whole sector: let residents help shape what the museum knows, preserves and values.

title: Watch David Bowie Take MTV to Task for Failing to Play Music Videos by Black Artists (1983)
content:
The old vaudeville phrase “Will it play in Peoria?” has its roots in the late 19th century, specifically in Horatio Alger’s novel Five Hundred Dollars; Or Jacob Marlowe’s Secret. Like all of the books Alger wrote extolling the virtues of thrift, study, grooming, industry, etc., this one articulates a middle American bootstraps philosophy and rags-to-riches mythology, while giving the entertainment industry a colorful way to sum up the small-town audiences who embraced Alger’s strait-laced ethic, and who needed to be pandered to or they wouldn’t get all those big-city jokes and references.

Peoria has been many places in the U.S.—from Tulsa to Boise—but whatever the test market, the assumptions have always been the same: the American mainstream is insular, middle class or aspiring to it, culturally conservative, unfailingly white, and fearful of everyone who isn’t. Such demographic dogma has persisted for over a hundred years. Even when it is shown to be outmoded or plain wrong, broadcasters and journalists continue to play to Peoria, genuflecting to a static, populist version of the U.S. that ignores large, rapidly changing segments of the population.

title: Mistral CEO: Europe faces ‘complete trap’ without frontier AI
content:
BERLIN — Europe risks falling into a “complete trap” if it focuses on industrial AI while leaving frontier models to the U.S. and China, Mistral CEO Arthur Mensch said in an interview Monday.

On the sidelines of the Digital Summit in Berlin, Mensch said Europe needs to build its own computing capacity and advanced AI models to ensure security. He added that Europe cannot assume it will always have access to the most powerful foreign models, pointing to the risk that the U.S. and China could deploy export controls on AI.

“The idea that we can build anything meaningful without owning the foundation of it, which are the reasoning models, the brains that can operate the factories, that can help design better systems … is, I think, a complete trap,” he said. “And we’re lucky that people realize this now, that this is not a viable way.”

In recent weeks, Mensch has emerged as a leading voice against European leaders’ shift away from building frontier AI models. In September, top EU leaders advocated building applications on foreign models to reap the benefits, instead of chasing frontier models.

title: COP31 explained: Why the Türkiye climate summit matters
content:

COP31 comes after a year in which the climate crisis has become even harder to ignore. In September 2026, the United Nations acknowledged for the first time that the world is set to overshoot its target of limiting global warming to 1.5°C above pre-industrial levels within the next few years. The warning came as global temperatures continued to soar with the last two months setting global heat records.

title: All Souls or just your cat's?
content: On All Saints' Day (1 November) and All Souls' Day (2 November), millions of Europeans visit cemeteries and light candles in memory of the dead. But few believe the dead can still reach them. While the dead are remembered in this Christian tradition that dates back to the 10th century, few people today believe the dead can still reach out to the living. But what about animals? A Pew Research survey across 10 countries found that people are often more likely to believe that living animals have spirits than to believe the spirits of their dead ancestors can help or harm them. The gap is the biggest in Türkiye, where 81% believe living animals have spirits while 21% think our ancestors can still reach us. In Spain, most people don't believe in either. So don't forget to light a candle for all our furry friends who are still among us!

However, as Delfi’s investigation shows, some preparedness recommendations have been in place in many countries for years, while more recent information campaigns are linked to specific national civil protection and societal resilience plans, rather than an impending global catastrophe.

In October this year, posts began circulating on X, Threads and other social media platforms claiming that numerous countries around the world were, one after another, urging residents to prepare so-called 72-hour emergency bags or stocks of essential goods and supplies that would allow them to manage for at least three days without outside assistance. Reports that the US Department of Defense was planning to prepare military bases to operate for three months without external support added fuel to the fire.

These posts have reached very large audiences in a short time. For example, a post by an account called Whale News Daily on X has received more than 5.3 million views.

title: Voting Experts Feared “Chaos” on Election Day. So Far, It Hasn’t Materialized.
content:
As Americans cast ballots on Tuesday, voting experts’ deepest concerns largely didn’t materialize on a mostly routine Election Day.

Tuesday’s relative quiet followed an anxious run-up in which the Trump administration pressed forward with unprecedented efforts to assert more federal control over elections.

Since President Donald Trump retook the White House, his administration has tried to force states to turn over their unredacted voter rolls and to restrict mail-in voting. The Department of Homeland Security has used its resources to identify and prosecute noncitizen voters, an effort that has unfolded alongside the agency’s massive crackdown on immigrants.

The president has justified these steps by claiming, without evidence, that American elections are beset by fraud and that illegal voting is tipping the scales in favor of Democrats.

ProPublica’s reporters are on the lookout for what’s going right and what isn’t. We’re monitoring voter suppression and interference, election observers and poll watchers, extremism tied to the election, and ICE activity at the polls. Have you seen something?

Tällä viikolla Euroopan parlamentin valiokunnissa käsitellään muun muassa puolustusta ja sotilaallista liikkuvuutta, muuttoliikettä ja rajaturvallisuutta, EU:n laajentumista, pitkän aikavälin talousarviota, ilmastopolitiikkaa sekä digitaalista lainsäädäntöä. Maanantaina EU:n ulkoasioiden ja turvallisuuspolitiikan korkea edustaja Kaja Kallas isännöi EU:n ja Yhdistyneen kuningaskunnan välistä turvallisuus- ja puolustuspoliittista vuoropuhelua. Komission puheenjohtaja Ursula von der Leyen puolestaan tapaa eurooppalaisten startup-yritysten toimitusjohtajia ja kestävän kehityksen sidosryhmiä. title: Tuttu suku kärvistelee ja selviää Kinnusen uudessa romaanissa
content:
Eero Karisto

Uudessa romaanissaan Pitkä aukea Tommi Kinnunen jatkaa aiemmista romaaneista tutun suvun tarinaa. Vaikka kirjan maailmassa on paljon ilkeyttä ja vaikeutta, yleisvaikutelma on positiivinen. Kaikesta selvitään.

Suku tuli tutuksi jo Kinnusen esikoisessa Neljäntienristeys, ja se tavattiin myös romaanissa Lopotti.

Pitkän aukean taustalla vaikuttaa jatkuvasti jo esikoisessa kerrottu isän seksuaalinen suuntautuminen ja siihen liittynyt itsemurha. Homoseksuaalisuus on muutenkin näkyvästi läsnä Kinnusen tuotannossa.

Pitkän aukean kertojan, tuon itsensä tappaneen miehen pojan ajatukset kiertävät isän ympärillä, lapsuuden muistoissa, niissä iloisissa mutta myös todella surkeissa. Romaanissa isä tuntuu olevan enemmän läsnä kuin omat lapset. Kertojan ja isän suhde elää vain kertojan ajatuksissa. Omat lapset tuntuvat tietävän kovin vähän ennen heidän syntymäänsä kuolleesta isoisästä.

Osa romaanin tarinaa on ilkeän anopin ja ihan normaalin, jopa kärsivällisen miniän jännite. Kertojan sympatiat ovat täysin varauksetta puolison puolella. Äiti on yksiselitteisesti suvun pahis.

title: Berlin unveils blueprint to catch up on AI
content:
BERLIN — Germany is unveiling its plan to catch up in the global AI race, but key details remain unclear.

Germany should become a “sovereign AI nation” by 2030 and narrow the gap with leading AI hubs in the U.S. and China, according to a report drafted by the government’s AI task force and obtained by POLITICO set to be released Monday.

“The next 12 to 18 months will therefore be decisive in setting the course,” read the report, which was due to be presented to the National Security Council and also at a summit on AI in Berlin.

Germany wants to secure access to the world’s leading models while strengthening European alternatives, particularly through expanded cooperation with France and Canada, according to the report. 

“We are leveraging collaborations with like-minded partners in the EU and worldwide (especially France and Canada) to benefit the German AI ecosystem and ensure sovereign access,” the report noted. “We will also use intra-European collaborations,” such as with French AI company Mistral, “to achieve this leverage,” its authors added.

At the same time, “AI made in Germany” should stand out through its focus on industrial AI with “highly specialized models,” the report read.

title: Frontex is eyeing sweeping new powers
content: The EU's border agency Frontex should take charge of deporting migrants, the European Commission said last week. This would put an agency once accused of serious human rights violations at the heart of enforcing new rules to “return” or expel people who haven't been granted the right to stay in the EU. The tougher EU talk on migration follows a harsher stance from right-wing parties who teamed up earlier this year to agree on the Returns Regulation to detain non-EU nationals who have been ordered to leave. They would then be sent to so-called “return hubs”, such as a centre in Albania for people expelled from Italy who can't be deported to an unsafe home country. Frontex currently cooperates with EU governments to remove people from the EU. It worked with them on some 64,000 returns last year, of which 65% were voluntary and 35% forced. It chartered more than 220 flights and reintegrated some 20,000 people back into their home country, which frequently involves paying them to leave Europe. The Commission foresees Frontex becoming far bigger and taking on more responsibilities. It wants to triple the corps to 30,000, including 6,000 Frontex staff, 7,000 officers seconded by EU
