title: Tribal Leaders Warned Border Wall Construction Would Disturb Native American Remains. They Were Right.
content:
Lorraine Eiler stood in the blazing August sun, surrounded by reporters, to offer a warning. The Trump administration was racing to erect a second border wall across Organ Pipe Cactus National Monument, southwest of Tucson. If the bulldozers came, she said, they were bound to disturb the final resting places of her family and Hia-Ced O’odham tribal ancestors.

“People used to live here,” the 89-year-old said.

Fifteen days later, her fears were realized.

ProPublica has confirmed that Native American remains were unearthed in Organ Pipe amid soil overturned by border wall contractors.

The discovery, unreported until now, was made on Sept. 8, the National Park Service said in a statement. “Following established protocols, the University of Arizona conducted an assessment and confirmed that the remains are human and align with tribal cremation practices,” the agency said.

The Native American Graves Protection and Repatriation Act governs the steps agencies must take following an inadvertent discovery of Native American remains on federal land. Those steps include halting any activity that contributed to the discovery until tribal communities are consulted.

title: Modern warfare spurs demand for new medical techniques
content:
Russia’s attacks on Ukraine’s health system and the changing nature of warfare have prompted innovative ways to protect wounded soldiers on the battlefield. 

From drone injuries and evacuations to fears of chemical, biological, nuclear or radiation attacks, there’s a major need for new technology and techniques to better support fighters — and citizens — caught in modern war zones.

Although banned under international law, attacks on health care facilities have become commonplace. The Kremlin has attacked health care facilities more than 3,000 times since the start of its full-scale invasion of Ukraine, according to World Health Organization data — and it continues to destroy critical health supplies.

In addition, double tap strikes — when a second attack is launched against people going to help those injured in the first — have also increased the risks health care personnel face on the battlefield. 

These new warfare tactics serve to psychologically break those fighting to protect Ukraine, former U.S. Navy SEAL Marcus Luttrell said. “To completely break down the society, you get rid of the energy and then the health care,” said Luttrell, a former Navy medic.

title: Pretty privilege can save lives
content: There’s the yellow swallowtail, a large, bright yellow butterfly with a stunning tail. Then there are less eye-catching species, such as the Alpine grayling – a rather plain-looking, brown butterfly found in the Alps. Recently, more than 21,000 people from over 100 countries took part in a survey rating almost 500 European butterfly species. Their responses were used to create a “beauty index”. Bright colours, particularly yellow and blue, contrasting patterns, and large, serrated wings or tails scored highest. The species that scored highest also had more photos on Flickr and iNaturalist, and more Wikipedia views. They also had more genetic studies and published research. “We had expected this to be the case in terms of public perception,” said Elisabeth Kühn from the Helmholtz Centre for Environmental Research (UFZ), who coordinated this survey for Germany, in a press release. “However, we were surprised to find the same pattern in scientific research.” It’s not just a butterfly thing. Because three small Baltic countries have a population of 5.7 million (and a combined area smaller than that of some second-tier Chinese city), half of whom live in Europe, while another third are Russians who cannot obtain citizenship, and because they have trauma and bad memories of Soviet rule, the entire world of eight billion people is supposed to head towards a nuclear apocalypse and perish,” Branko Milanović wrote on X on the 19th of October.

title: Ukrainian could become Lithuania’s second official language – fake news circulated in the names of officials
content:
A fabricated news item circulating on Lithuanian social media appears to show President Gitanas Nausėda and Foreign Minister Kęstutis Budrys expressing views on the possibility of granting Ukrainian the status of a second official language. How was it established that the material was generated by artificial intelligence?

The fake report claims, citing alleged statements by Nausėda and Budrys, that they do not rule out the possibility of Ukrainian becoming Lithuania’s second official language and being made compulsory in schools.

According to Delfi.lt, the image circulating on social media attempts to imitate an article published by the news portal 15min, but was created using artificial intelligence. This is evidenced not only by the fact that the man pictured next to the president bears little resemblance to the foreign minister, but also by a digital watermark embedded in the image.

title: EU and Canada’s 6-month test of commitment
content:
MONTREAL, Canada — The European Union and Canada have agreed to build the closest possible relationship. Over the next six months, they will have to define what that means — and whether Canada can become the EU’s first, and perhaps only, associate member.

A summit in Montreal last week highlighted the urgency behind the budding relationship. Both sides say their partnership is positive and not directed against any country. But it is also driven by mutual need: to shore up supply chains, pool expertise and reduce reliance on the United States and China.

Mark Carney told POLITICO in an interview straight after the summit that the two sides should not be tailoring their partnership to cope with the potential reactions of other powers. “We’re not adjusting [based on] what the U.S. might think, what China might think, what … Russia might think,” he said. The goal, the Canadian prime minister explained, is to help both sides “withstand shocks” and prevent rivals from exploiting critical dependencies.

title: Australia: Solitary Confinement Harming Prisoners with Disabilities
content:
(Sydney) — Prison authorities in the Australian state of South Australia are harming people with disabilities by using solitary confinement, Human Rights Watch said in a report released today.

The 50-page report, “‘They Just Locked Me Away’: Solitary Confinement and Abuse of People with Disabilities in Prisons in the State of South Australia,” documents the use of solitary confinement on people with psychosocial disabilities, mental health conditions. It details broader problems facing people with disabilities in South Australian prisons, including inadequate access to individualized mental health care and lack of prison oversight.

content:
YK:n ikääntyneiden oikeuksien sopimuksen sisällöllistä valmisteluprosessia jatkettiin hallitusten välisissä neuvotteluissa Genevessä 26.–30.10.2026. Tulevan ihmisoikeussopimuksen sopimuskohtia tullaan valmistelemaan jäsenvaltioiden edustajien vetämissä temaattisissa työryhmissä. Työskentelyyn osallistetaan niin kansalaisjärjestöt, ikääntyneet ihmiset kuin kansalliset ihmisoikeusinstituutiot.

Uusi ihmisoikeussopimus tulee vahvistamaan ikääntyneiden ihmisoikeuksia ja paikkaamaan kansainvälisen oikeuden aukkoja. Kansalliset ihmisoikeusinstituutiot painottivat lokakuun valmisteluistonnon edellä, että lähtökohtana uuden kansainvälisen sopimuksen valmistelussa on tunnistaa rakenteissa olevat ikääntyneisiin kohdistuvat ennakkoluulot, yhteiskunnallinen eriarvoisuus ja eri syrjinnän muodot.

Kansalliset ihmisoikeusinstituutiot korostivat istunnossa, että koko prosessin pitää olla läpinäkyvä. Kansalaisyhteiskunnan, ikääntyneiden ihmisten ja kansallisten ihmisoikeusinstituutioiden vahvan osallistamisen lisäksi valmistelu vaatii laajaa osallistumista ja tukea myös YK:n jäsenvaltioilta.

title: Digital Independence Day: Towards the open social web
content:
Does your organisation use Facebook, Instagram or X? Every day you stay there, you make your audience more dependent on data-guzzling platforms with addictive algorithms, without knowing whether people actually get to see your content. So it’s high time to start using alternatives where you’re in control!

On the open social web, you can also reach your audience through platforms that aren’t owned by a single company, and where people have a choice. By sharing your posts there too, you make your audience less dependent on the commercial platforms.

title: Beirutin taivas ei ole enää hiljainen
content:
Israelin droonit surisevat Libanonin yllä tulitauoista huolimatta. Parhaimmillaan ne valvovat naapurustoja, keräävät tietoa ja painostavat väestöä. Pahimmillaan ne iskevät tekoälyn avulla kohteisiin ja ihmisiin, joita Israel pitää uhkana. Libanonin kokemus antaa esimakua tulevaisuuden sodankäynnistä, jolla ei ole selvää loppua: se jatkuu valvontana ja psykologisena painostuksena, eikä kukaan joudu siitä tilille.

Kun koneeni laskeutui syyskuussa Beirutiin ja istuin taksissa matkalla keskustaan, huomasin jotain outoa. Taivaalta ei kuulunut Israelin droonien matalaa surinaa. Hiljaisuus osoittautui kuitenkin tilapäiseksi.

title: Human speech follows the same patterns as birdsong — new research
content:
In every culture, humans speak and sing to each other. We have created an astounding array of languages and musical structures across the globe. And yet, within this diversity, some fundamental sequence patterns are repeated. These are often referred to as “universal” patterns in human vocalization.

Our new research, published this week in Science, reveals that many of these acoustic patterns in human song and speech are also shared with birdsong.

The study compared the songs of 367 bird species with examples of song and speech from 52 human languages.

As researchers in animal behaviour and neuroscience and music, we (Logan and Jon) spent 10 years documenting the prevalence of universal human acoustic patterns in the songs of zebra finches.

When Kendra joined our lab during her PhD, she proposed we investigate whether these patterns are shared across other bird species as well.

title: ‘Apologies for any confusion!’: how to write the perfect passive-aggressive email
content:
In a survey, ‘just to be clear’ came out as the most loathed phrase. But I think I can do better

A new contender for the most passive-aggressive email phrase has emerged. “Just to be clear” was chosen by 52% of desk jockeys in a survey by email verification company ZeroBounce, closely followed by the perennial pass-ag fave, “per my last email” (40%), which tied with the identical-in-intent “as previously discussed”. Further down the list came “for future reference” and “kindly note”.

If you ask me, these all verge on actual aggressive. Imagine saying “just to be clear” out loud to another person: that’s a conversational poke in the ribs, isn’t it? It’s the kind of thing you unleash 10 minutes into an ill-tempered wrangle with your home insurance company about inflated renewal premiums. “Kindly note” is even worse – it’s a phrase from an angry message on the office kitchen wall about microwave abuse.

title: Forget AI, Europe has a plan to win the next tech revolution
content:
Draft strategy on quantum computing obtained by POLITICO shows Europe won’t repeat its AI regulatory playbook.

By PIETER HAECK
in Brussels

Illustration by Nicolás Ortega for POLITICO

A perennial also-ran in the global AI race, Europe now sees an opportunity to win what promises to be another technological revolution by learning from its mistakes.

Brussels is set to unveil the Quantum Act, a major piece of tech-sector legislation aimed at pushing EU countries to band together to attempt to stay ahead of the United States and China in quantum computing.

A draft of the November proposal obtained by POLITICO seeks to overcome factors that have constrained Europe’s ambitions in artificial intelligence, including a lack of funding to turn research into commercially viable and competitive products — and to scale globally.

Crucially, it also shifts focus away from regulating the technology to driving competitiveness — an acknowledgement of concerns that Europe overregulated AI and shouldn’t do the same in a field in which it is at the scientific forefront.

title: In Kazakhstan, rural women are forming collectives to improve their livelihoods
content:
Their most pressing challenge is solving the long-standing water shortage in the village

Originally published on Global Voices

Participants of the project in Qyzylsay, Kazakhstan. Photo by Nazgul Aidabossynova. Used with permission.

This interview is part of a series of spotlights on the work of some of the grantees of the Digital Spark granting scheme, as part of the Regional Support Mechanism EECA project, implemented by the Metamorphosis Foundation and TechSoup, in partnership with CIVICUS and under the Digital Democracy Initiative (DDI) that covers the Global South. It is being published on Global Voices as part of a content-sharing agreement.  

Women in the rural areas of Kazakhstan are among those most affected by climate change, energy deficit, and poor governance. They bear the heavy burden of water shortages, especially in the southern parts of the country, where this problem is the most acute due to dense population, economic reliance on agriculture, and water losses related to outdated irrigation infrastructure.

title: OPINION: How to Stop the US-Israel War on Iran
content:
Arab states must reject Israeli hegemony and build a regional security framework independent of Washington.

By Jeffrey D. Sachs and Sybil Fares

NEW YORK | 31 October 2026 (IDN) — The war that Israel and the United States launched against Iran on 28 February is in a lull, not at an end. Major combat has paused, diplomacy has stalled, and both sides are preparing for the next round. To understand why the fighting will soon resume, we need to understand the motivations of the two governments that started it. Neither of them wants peace. Israel’s leadership seeks domination over the Middle East, and the United States seeks to preserve its domination over the world. Stating these aims underscores that both governments operate in a delusional world.

title: YK:n luontokokouksen viesti on selvä: luontokadon pysäyttäminen vaatii lisärahoitusta ja toimien kiihdyttämistä
content:
YK:n luontokokouksessa päästiin yhteisymmärrykseen osassa merkittävistä rahoituskysymyksissä luontokadon pysäyttämiseksi, mutta rahoitusta tarvitaan lisää. Rahavirtoja on ohjattava uudelleen esimerkiksi luonnolle haitallisia tukia uudistamalla.

Tänään aamulla päättyneessä YK:n COP17 -luontokokouksessa onnistuttiin säilyttämään vuoden 2030 luontotavoitteet ja sopimaan toimeenpanon vauhdittamisesta. Tämä on tärkeä saavutus vaikeassa geopoliittisessa tilanteessa.

Maailman valtiot sitoutuivat pysäyttämään luontokadon vuoteen 2030 mennessä neljä vuotta sitten Montrealissa. Jerevanin kokouksen tavoitteena oli panna vauhtia tavoitteen saavuttamiseen. Luontokadon pysäyttämiseksi vaadittavasta rahoituksesta sopiminen kuului kokouksen vaikeimpien kysymysten listalle ja se jäi osittain edelleen ratkaisematta.

"Ilman selvää lisäystä rahoitus tulee jatkossakin olemaan YK:n luontokokousten ratkaisematon kysymys. Haasteena on löytää riittävät resurssit tavoitteiden saavuttamiseen ja samalla ohjata rahavirtoja pois luontokatoa kiihdyttävästä toiminnasta”, sanoo WWF:n kansainvälisen ohjelman johtaja Anne Tarvainen.
